field.summary: Retention window for admin activity log entries; older ones are pruned.
field.usage: How long admin activity log entries are kept before cleanup removes them. The field note asks for a number of days; a shorter window keeps the log table small, a longer one preserves more audit history for investigations.

field.summary: Turns admin activity logging on or off.
field.usage: When Yes, actions performed by admin users are recorded to the admin activity log. Set to No to stop collecting this log.

field.summary: Whether admin login activity is recorded.
field.usage: When Yes, admin user sign-in activity is captured in the admin activity log.

field.summary: Whether admin page visits are recorded.
field.usage: When Yes, the admin pages visited by admin users are captured in the admin activity log.

field.summary: Whether admin CAPTCHA answers must match letter case.
field.usage: When Yes, the entered CAPTCHA text must match the case of the displayed characters. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA in Admin is set to Yes.

field.summary: Turns the built-in image CAPTCHA on or off for Admin Panel forms.
field.usage: When Yes, the legacy image CAPTCHA is required on the selected admin forms; No disables it. Applies to the Admin Panel.

field.summary: Failed-login threshold before the admin CAPTCHA appears; 0 means it is always shown.
field.usage: Number of failed admin logins allowed before CAPTCHA is required. Applies only when admin CAPTCHA is enabled and set to show after failures. Lower values block brute-force attempts sooner; as the native note says, 0 shows CAPTCHA on every login attempt.

field.summary: The font used to render the admin CAPTCHA image.
field.usage: Selects which configured font the CAPTCHA characters are drawn with. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA in Admin is set to Yes.

field.summary: Which Admin Panel forms display the CAPTCHA.
field.usage: Selects the admin forms (such as login and forgot password) that require a CAPTCHA. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA in Admin is set to Yes.

field.summary: Number of CAPTCHA characters (max 8, range allowed); higher is harder for bots and humans.
field.usage: How many characters the CAPTCHA challenge shows (8 max; a range like 3-5 randomises the count). More characters make it harder for bots but also for people. Applies only when CAPTCHA is enabled.

field.summary: When the admin CAPTCHA is shown — e.g. always or after failed attempts.
field.usage: Chooses when a CAPTCHA is required, such as always or only after a number of failed login attempts. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA in Admin is set to Yes.

values.value: Always show the CAPTCHA.

value.label: After number of attempts to login

values.value: Show the CAPTCHA only after a number of failed attempts.

field.summary: The character pool CAPTCHA images are drawn from; applies only when CAPTCHA is enabled.
field.usage: Defines which characters can appear in generated CAPTCHA images. The field note restricts this to letters and digits and warns that look-alike characters lower recognition. Applies only when admin CAPTCHA is enabled.

field.summary: How many minutes a displayed admin CAPTCHA stays valid before expiring.
field.usage: The lifetime, in minutes, of a displayed CAPTCHA before a new one must be generated. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA in Admin is set to Yes.

field.summary: Whether charts are displayed on the Admin dashboard.
field.usage: When Yes, the Admin dashboard renders its sales/order charts. Disabling can reduce load on large stores where the chart queries are heavy.

field.summary: Which store email identity sends Admin password forgot/reset emails.
field.usage: The sender identity for Admin 'forgot password' and reset emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2).

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Template used for the admin forgot-password email.
field.usage: The email template sent when an admin user requests a password reset. As the field note says, the Default option resolves through theme fallback; pick a custom template to override the wording or branding of that message.

field.summary: Email template for notifying a newly created admin user.
field.usage: The template for the email sent to a newly created admin user. As the native note says, Default follows theme fallback. Global scope.

field.summary: Template for admin-user notification emails; pick a custom one to override the theme default.
field.usage: Selects the email template for admin user notification messages. A custom template overrides the theme default, which is used when 'Default' is selected.

field.summary: Caps the product count loaded into the admin grid to speed it up on large catalogs.
field.usage: When Yes, limits how many products the admin grid collection loads. On large catalogs this noticeably speeds up the grid, but reported totals and some filtering become approximate. When No, the full count is used. Global scope.

field.summary: Caps products loaded in the admin grid to keep large catalogs responsive (minimum 20000).
field.usage: Caps how many products the admin product grid loads so very large catalogs stay responsive; the minimum is 20000. Applies only when limiting the total number of products in the grid is enabled.

field.summary: No blocks concurrent logins to one admin account (more secure); Yes allows the same account from multiple machines.
field.usage: When No (the safer default, per the note), a new login elsewhere ends the existing session, so an admin account can't be used from two machines at once. Yes permits concurrent sessions — needed only when a team genuinely shares one login. Default scope.

field.summary: Failed admin logins before lockout; lower is safer but risks locking out admins, empty disables it.
field.usage: How many consecutive failed admin logins trigger an account lockout. A lower number hardens against brute-force attempts but risks locking out legitimate admins; leaving it empty disables lockout entirely.

field.summary: How long, in minutes, an admin account stays locked after too many failed logins.
field.usage: The duration, in minutes, that an admin account is locked once the failed-login limit is reached, after which sign-in is allowed again.

field.summary: Caps admin password-reset requests per hour to curb abuse; 0 disables the limit. Tied to the chosen reset-protection type.
field.usage: Limits how many admin password-reset requests are accepted per hour, throttling abuse and denial-of-service attempts (native note). Set 0 to disable the cap. Applies under the selected password reset protection type (depends). Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Throttles repeated admin password-reset requests to curb abuse; 0 disables the delay.
field.usage: Minimum delay, in minutes, between successive password-reset requests, limiting abuse and email flooding. Use 0 to disable. Applies only under the matching password-reset protection type.

field.summary: Shortest allowed admin password; longer minimums resist brute-force guessing. The enforced floor is 7 characters.
field.usage: Sets the minimum character count for admin passwords, applied whenever one is set or changed. Longer minimums make admin accounts harder to brute-force. The native note states values below 7 are rejected. Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Whether a periodic admin password change is forced or only recommended.
field.usage: Chooses whether admins are required to change their password once the password lifetime elapses, or merely prompted to. Governs how the password-expiry policy is applied.

values.value: Admins are prompted to change their password but not forced.
Admins are forced to change their password on the schedule.

field.summary: Days before an admin password must be changed; leave empty to disable expiry.
field.usage: The number of days an admin password stays valid before the user must change it. As the field note says, leaving the field empty disables password expiry entirely, so admins are never forced to rotate.

field.summary: Hours an admin password-recovery link stays valid; shorter limits the window a leaked link can be used.
field.usage: How many hours an admin password-reset link remains usable before it expires (enter 1 or more, per the note). Shorter periods reduce the window in which an intercepted or forwarded recovery link could reset an admin password. Default scope.

field.summary: How admin password-reset requests are rate-limited — by IP, email, both, or not at all.
field.usage: Limits admin forgot-password requests by By IP and Email, By IP, By Email, or None, to throttle abuse of the password-reset flow.

values.value: Rate-limit password resets by both IP address and email.
Rate-limit password resets by IP address.
Rate-limit password resets by email address.
Do not rate-limit password resets.

field.summary: How long an idle admin stays signed in; shorter is safer but logs admins out more often.
field.usage: Idle time, in seconds, before an admin session expires and the user must log in again. Shorter values limit the risk of unattended sessions; longer values are more convenient but less secure. Must be between 60 and 31536000 (one year).

field.summary: Whether Admin usernames are matched case-sensitively at login.
field.usage: When Yes, Admin login treats the username as case-sensitive; when No, case is ignored.

field.summary: Adds a secret key to Admin URLs to protect against cross-site request forgery.
field.usage: When Yes, Admin URLs include a per-session secret key, a CSRF protection. Leave enabled unless a specific integration requires otherwise.

field.summary: The Admin page shown first after a user signs in.
field.usage: The landing page displayed when an Admin user logs in, chosen from the available Admin menu destinations.

field.summary: Selects which installed theme is used for the Admin panel interface.
field.usage: Chooses the active Admin theme from the themes installed for the backend, changing the look of the Admin panel.

field.summary: Overrides the admin host/URL; a wrong value can lock you out of admin, and it takes effect only after a cache flush.
field.usage: Replaces the base URL used for the admin panel (applies only when Use Custom Admin URL is enabled). It must end in a slash and point at a URL that actually serves Magento, since a wrong value locks you out of admin. The change takes effect after the configuration cache is flushed.

field.summary: Replaces the default /admin path with a custom one; you are signed out and must re-login after saving.
field.usage: Changes the admin panel's URL path for obscurity, so the panel no longer answers at the default address. Applies only when 'Use Custom Admin Path' is enabled. After saving you are logged out and must sign in at the new path, and old bookmarks break.

field.summary: Whether the Admin panel is served from a custom base URL.
field.usage: When Yes, the Admin uses a custom base URL instead of the default. Set the URL in the related field. Misconfiguration can lock you out of the Admin.

field.summary: Whether the Admin is reached at a custom path instead of the default.
field.usage: When Yes, the Admin is accessed under a custom path (e.g. /myadmin) rather than the default. Set the path in the related field. Misconfiguration can lock you out of the Admin.

field.summary: Sends anonymized admin-UI usage telemetry to Magento; turn off if your data-privacy policy forbids outbound tracking.
field.usage: Beyond opting into usage tracking, this streams anonymized data about how admins use the panel back to Magento/Adobe. Turn it off (No) where your data-privacy policy forbids outbound telemetry. It affects neither the storefront nor store performance.

field.summary: Scheduled retranslation overwrites manual product-translation edits on the next cron run; can differ per store view.
field.usage: The native note warns it overwrites manual edits. The mechanism: retranslation runs on a schedule via cron, so any hand-corrected product translation is replaced the next time the job runs. Leave it No if editors maintain translations by hand. Scoped per website/store view.

field.summary: Set to No to skip URL rewrite generation during automatic translation and save performance; translated URLs then need rebuilding separately.
field.usage: Yes/No. Controls whether URL rewrites are generated for translated URLs during automatic translation. Setting No saves processing time, but newly translated-language URLs stay unbrowsable until you regenerate the rewrites by another means. Can be set per website and store view.

field.summary: How often product translations are processed; too frequent adds API load, too rare delays new translations.
field.usage: Schedule, in Unix crontab syntax, for the batch job that translates product data. Tighter intervals pick up changes sooner but add translation-API calls and server load; wider intervals save cost but delay new translations. The expression is validated before saving.

field.summary: Days before an already-translated product is retranslated; lower means more frequent, costlier re-runs.
field.usage: Sets how stale a translation may get before periodic retranslation redoes it, measured from each product's Last translation date. A shorter period keeps catalog copy fresher but triggers more translation-engine calls and cost. Applies only when periodic retranslation is enabled; website/store scoped.

field.summary: Picks which select/multiselect product attributes get their options auto-translated; set per store view.
field.usage: Chooses the select and multiselect product attributes whose options are automatically translated. As the field note says, empty options are always translated and the auto-retranslation toggle below has no effect here. Scoped to default/website/store, so each store view can translate a different set.

field.summary: Schedules the background job that translates select-attribute values; uses standard cron syntax.
field.usage: Cron schedule for the job that translates dropdown/select attribute values. The native note gives the syntax. Running it too frequently can run up translation-API calls and cost, while infrequent runs leave new values untranslated longer. Global (default) scope only.

field.summary: More selected attributes means more content sent to the translation engine — higher cost and processing time.
field.usage: Each attribute you pick here is sent to the translation engine, so adding more raises translation volume, cost and processing time. Only text attributes are eligible. Set per website or store view, so different locales can translate different fields.

field.summary: Yes lets the scheduled auto-translation also process disabled products, spending translation credits on items not on the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, the periodic automatic-translation run (not the manual button, per the note) also translates products that are disabled. Effect: translation-API calls and credits are spent on items that aren't visible on the storefront. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Shows the language texts are translated into — the target store view's configured Locale.
field.usage: Read-only indicator of the automatic-translation target language. It follows the Locale of the target store view (General > Locale options), so change the language there rather than here. Differs per store view.

field.summary: Turns AI automatic translation on or off.
field.usage: When Yes, the AI Integration automatic translation feature is active. Can be set per website or store view, so translation can run on some stores and not others.

field.summary: The base language the AI translates from; set it wrong and every translation starts from the wrong source text.
field.usage: Tells the translation engine which language your product data is already written in, so it translates from the correct base. Set it to the wrong language and otherwise-correct content gets mistranslated. Applies store-wide.

field.summary: DeepL API key used for translations; stored encrypted and only used when DeepL is the engine.
field.usage: The DeepL authentication key the module uses to call the translation API; the field note links where to create one. It is stored encrypted at rest, and applies only when the translation engine is set to DeepL.

field.summary: Chooses the external translation service; each engine has its own quality, cost and API credentials.
field.usage: Sets which external service performs all automatic translation (DeepL, OpenAI, etc.). Switching it changes translation quality and cost, and requires that engine's own API credentials to be configured. Store-wide setting.

field.summary: Credential for the Gemini engine; stored encrypted. Without a valid key, Gemini translation calls fail.
field.usage: API key used to authenticate with Google Gemini, stored encrypted. Used only when the translation engine is set to Google Gemini. If it is missing or invalid, translation requests to Gemini fail.

field.summary: Picks the Google Gemini model used for translation; options load after a valid API key is saved.
field.usage: Which Gemini model performs translations. Applies only when the translation engine is set to Google Gemini. The choice trades translation quality against speed and API cost; the list appears once a valid API key is saved, per the native note. Global scope.

field.summary: Credential for the OpenAI translation engine; stored encrypted and used only when that engine is selected.
field.usage: Authenticates calls to OpenAI for automatic translation. Entered as an obscured field and stored encrypted, and only used when the translation engine is set to OpenAI. Set at default scope — a single key serves all stores.

field.summary: Picks the OpenAI model used for translation; higher-tier models cost more per request and differ in quality and speed.
field.usage: Chooses which OpenAI model performs the translations. Options appear only after a valid API key and organization ID are saved. The choice trades translation quality against per-request cost and speed — see the linked OpenAI docs. Applies only when the OpenAI engine is selected.

field.summary: Only needed if your OpenAI account spans multiple organizations; used only when the OpenAI translation engine is selected.
field.usage: Set this only if your OpenAI account belongs to more than one organization and requests must be scoped/billed to a specific one; otherwise leave it blank to use your default org. Applies only when the OpenAI translation engine is selected.

field.summary: Scopes OpenAI usage and billing to one project; stored encrypted. Only used when the OpenAI translation engine is selected.
field.usage: The OpenAI project this store's translation calls are billed and tracked against; stored encrypted. Applies only when the translation engine is set to OpenAI. Left blank, OpenAI uses your default project (per the note), so set it to isolate spend or usage limits per project.

field.summary: The DHL account number used for rating and shipping.
field.usage: The DHL account number sent with rate and label requests. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Turns the DHL shipping method on or off at checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, DHL rates are offered to shoppers during checkout; No hides the carrier. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The DHL REST API key used to authenticate requests.
field.usage: Key used to authenticate requests to the DHL REST API. Stored encrypted and can be set per website.

field.summary: The DHL REST API secret used to authenticate requests.
field.usage: Secret paired with the API key to authenticate requests to the DHL REST API. Stored encrypted and can be set per website.

field.summary: Picks Documents vs Non-Documents service for international DHL shipments, which determines the rates quoted.
field.usage: Selects which DHL service — Documents or Non-Documents (per the note) — is used for non-domestic shipments, with EU shipments counted as domestic. The choice drives which rate set DHL returns, so the wrong type can produce wrong or missing rates. Set per website.

field.summary: Whether DHL request and response data is logged for troubleshooting.
field.usage: When Yes, DHL API requests and responses are written to the debug log. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The parcel depth sent to DHL for rating.
field.usage: The package depth used for DHL quotes. Applies only when Size is set to the regular/custom size. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Only matters for orders over DHL's 70 kg limit; Yes gets rates by splitting them into multiple packages.
field.usage: When Yes, DHL may split an order exceeding 70 kg into multiple packages to optimise shipping charges. Has no effect on orders under that weight. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Which DHL document (paperwork) shipping services are offered.
field.usage: Selects the DHL services available for document shipments. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The DHL service used for free shipping on document shipments.
field.usage: The DHL document service applied when an order qualifies for free shipping. Applies when the content type is Documents. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The DHL service used for free shipping on non-document shipments.
field.usage: The DHL parcel service applied when an order qualifies for free shipping. Applies when the content type is Non Documents. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Enables free DHL shipping once the order subtotal reaches a threshold.
field.usage: When enabled, DHL shipping is free for orders whose subtotal meets the Free Shipping Amount Threshold. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The order subtotal at which DHL shipping becomes free.
field.usage: Minimum order subtotal that qualifies for free DHL shipping. Applies only when Enable Free Shipping Threshold is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the DHL handling fee applies once per order or once per package, which changes the total on multi-package shipments.
field.usage: Per Order charges one handling fee for the whole order; Per Package charges the fee for each package (native note). The choice changes total handling cost whenever a shipment splits into multiple packages. Can differ per website.

values.value: Apply the handling fee once per order.
Apply the handling fee to each package.

field.summary: The handling fee added to DHL shipping charges.
field.usage: The amount or percentage added to each DHL quote, depending on how Calculate Handling Fee is set. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the DHL handling fee is a fixed amount or a percentage.
field.usage: Sets how the handling fee is calculated — as a fixed amount or as a percentage of the shipping cost. Can be set per website.

values.value: Add a fixed handling amount.
Add handling as a percentage of the rate.

field.summary: The parcel height sent to DHL for rating.
field.usage: The package height used for DHL quotes. Applies only when Size is set to the regular/custom size. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: The DHL Access ID used to authenticate API requests.
field.usage: Credential issued by DHL to authenticate rate and label requests. Stored encrypted and can be set per website.

field.summary: Which DHL non-document (parcel) shipping services are offered.
field.usage: Selects the DHL services available for non-document (parcel) shipments. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The DHL API password used to authenticate requests.
field.usage: Password paired with the DHL Access ID to authenticate API requests. Stored encrypted and can be set per website.

field.summary: Hours after order submission before a DHL package is ready; feeds DHL rate and transit quotes.
field.usage: Lead time in hours between order submission and the package being ready for DHL pickup. It shifts the ship date DHL uses when returning rate and transit-time quotes. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether DHL is offered to all allowed countries or only specific ones.
field.usage: Chooses between offering DHL to all allowed countries or to the specific list set in Ship to Specific Countries. Can be set per website.

values.value: Offer this method in every country your store already allows.
Limit this method to the specific countries you pick below.

field.summary: Whether DHL requests use the test (sandbox) environment instead of production.
field.usage: When Yes, DHL API calls use the sandbox/test endpoint for safe testing; No uses production. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether to still show DHL at checkout when it returns no rates.
field.usage: When Yes, DHL is shown with its error message even if no rates apply; No hides it. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Selects a regular or custom parcel size for DHL shipments.
field.usage: Chooses the parcel size sent to DHL; selecting the regular/custom option enables the Height, Depth and Width fields. Can be set per store view.

field.summary: The position of DHL in the list of shipping methods at checkout.
field.usage: Controls where DHL appears relative to other carriers; lower numbers sort first. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The countries DHL is offered to when limited to specific countries.
field.usage: The destination countries where DHL is available, used when Ship to Applicable Countries is set to specific countries. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The message shown to shoppers when DHL rates can't be retrieved.
field.usage: Text displayed at checkout when DHL returns no rates or an error. Can differ per store view.

technical.default_value: This shipping method is currently unavailable. If you would like to ship using this shipping method, please contact us.

field.summary: The carrier name shown to shoppers for DHL at checkout.
field.usage: The label displayed for this shipping method in the cart and checkout. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Selects which DHL web-service API is used to request rates and labels.
field.usage: Chooses the DHL integration used for quoting and shipping — the DHL XML or DHL REST API. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The weight unit used for package weights sent to DHL.
field.usage: The unit of measure applied when sending package weights to DHL. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: The parcel width sent to DHL for rating.
field.usage: The package width used for DHL quotes. Applies only when Size is set to the regular/custom size. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Your FedEx account for rate requests; stored encrypted. Use digits only, no dashes, or lookups fail.
field.usage: FedEx account ID used to authenticate rate requests, stored encrypted. Enter digits only with no dashes; a wrongly formatted value causes FedEx rate lookups to fail. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether FedEx shipping rates are offered to customers at checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, FedEx shipping methods are available as options during checkout. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Which FedEx shipping methods are offered to customers.
field.usage: Selects which FedEx shipping services are offered as options at checkout. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The FedEx API key used to authenticate rate and shipping requests.
field.usage: The API key from your FedEx developer account, used to authenticate requests to the FedEx web services. Stored encrypted. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether FedEx request and response data is logged for debugging.
field.usage: When Yes, FedEx API requests and responses are written to the debug log for troubleshooting. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether a separate set of credentials is used for the FedEx tracking API.
field.usage: When Yes, a separate set of FedEx tracking API credentials is used for shipment tracking requests, enabling the Tracking API Key and Secret fields. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The FedEx method used when an order qualifies for free shipping.
field.usage: Selects which FedEx shipping method is used when an order qualifies for free shipping. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether free shipping is offered once an order subtotal threshold is met.
field.usage: Set to Enable to offer FedEx free shipping for orders whose subtotal reaches the configured threshold. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The order subtotal required to qualify for free FedEx shipping.
field.usage: The minimum order subtotal at which FedEx free shipping becomes available. Applies only when Enable Free Shipping Threshold is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the handling fee is applied per order or per package.
field.usage: Chooses whether the handling fee is applied once per order or to each package. Can be set per website.

values.value: Apply the handling fee once per order.
Apply the handling fee to each package.

field.summary: The handling fee amount or percentage added to FedEx rates.
field.usage: The handling fee value added to FedEx shipping rates, interpreted as a fixed amount or percentage per the Calculate Handling Fee setting. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the handling fee is a fixed amount or a percentage.
field.usage: Chooses whether the handling fee added to FedEx rates is calculated as a fixed amount or as a percentage. Can be set per website.

values.value: Add a fixed handling amount.
Add handling as a percentage of the rate.

field.summary: The maximum weight allowed for a single FedEx package.
field.usage: The maximum weight of a single package for FedEx shipments; heavier orders are split across packages. Consult FedEx for the maximum supported weight. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The default FedEx packaging type assumed for rate requests.
field.usage: Selects the FedEx packaging type assumed when requesting shipping rates. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The FedEx pickup method used when requesting rates.
field.usage: Selects the FedEx pickup type, i.e. how packages are handed to FedEx, used when requesting shipping rates. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The FedEx production web-services endpoint URL.
field.usage: The endpoint URL for the FedEx production web services. Applies only when Sandbox Mode is set to No. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether shipments are rated as residential deliveries.
field.usage: When Yes, FedEx rates are requested for residential delivery, which may change the price. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether FedEx ships to all allowed countries or only selected ones.
field.usage: Chooses whether FedEx shipping is offered to all allowed countries or only to a specific list set in Ship to Specific Countries. Can be set per website.

values.value: Offer this method in every country your store already allows.
Limit this method to the specific countries you pick below.

field.summary: Whether requests use the FedEx sandbox (test) environment instead of production.
field.usage: When Yes, FedEx requests are sent to the sandbox (test) environment rather than production. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The FedEx sandbox (test) web-services endpoint URL.
field.usage: The endpoint URL for the FedEx sandbox (test) web services. Applies only when Sandbox Mode is set to Yes. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The FedEx API secret key used with the API key to authenticate requests.
field.usage: The API secret associated with your FedEx API key, used to authenticate requests to the FedEx web services. Stored encrypted. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether rates are requested per package or for all packages together.
field.usage: Chooses how package data is sent to FedEx when requesting rates — divided into separate packages or as a single combined request. Can be set per website.

values.value: Split the cart into equal weights and send one rate request.
Use the real package weight and send a request per package.

field.summary: Whether the FedEx method is still shown when it is not available for an order.
field.usage: When Yes, the FedEx shipping method is displayed at checkout even when it is not applicable, shown with the error message. Can be set per website.

field.summary: FedEx-assigned SmartPost hub ID; required for SmartPost shipments.
field.usage: The FedEx-assigned hub ID used for SmartPost shipments. Only relevant when the SmartPost method is selected; without a valid hub ID, SmartPost rate requests and labels fail. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The position of FedEx among shipping methods at checkout.
field.usage: A numeric value controlling where FedEx appears relative to other carriers in the checkout list; lower values appear first. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The specific countries FedEx shipping is offered to.
field.usage: Selects the countries to which FedEx shipping is offered when Ship to Applicable Countries is limited to specific countries. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The message shown to customers when FedEx rates cannot be retrieved.
field.usage: The error message displayed at checkout when FedEx shipping rates are unavailable. Can be set per website or store view.

technical.default_value: This shipping method is currently unavailable. If you would like to ship using this shipping method, please contact us.

field.summary: The carrier name shown to customers for FedEx shipping at checkout.
field.usage: The label displayed to customers for the FedEx carrier group at checkout. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The FedEx API key used for shipment tracking requests.
field.usage: The API key used to authenticate FedEx shipment tracking requests. Applies only when Enable Tracking API credentials is set to Yes. Stored encrypted.

field.summary: The FedEx API secret used for shipment tracking requests.
field.usage: The API secret used with the tracking API key to authenticate FedEx tracking requests. Applies only when Enable Tracking API credentials is Yes. Stored encrypted.

field.summary: The weight unit used for package weights sent to FedEx.
field.usage: Selects the weight unit used for package weights in FedEx rate requests. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Turns the Flat Rate shipping method on or off at checkout.
field.usage: When set to Yes, the Flat Rate carrier is offered at checkout. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The handling fee added to the Flat Rate shipping charge.
field.usage: The handling fee amount added to Flat Rate shipping, applied according to Calculate Handling Fee. Can be set per website.

field.summary: How the Flat Rate handling fee is calculated.

field.summary: The countries Free Shipping is offered to when limited to specific countries.

field.usage: The error text displayed to customers when Free Shipping cannot be offered for their order. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: The heading shown for the Free Shipping carrier at checkout.
field.usage: The carrier title displayed above the Free Shipping method at checkout. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Whether the In-Store Delivery (in-store pickup) shipping method is offered at checkout.

field.summary: How far from the customer the storefront searches for pickup stores; larger finds more but less local.
field.usage: Radius, in kilometres, used to find in-store pickup locations during storefront checkout. A larger radius surfaces more stores but may list distant ones; a smaller radius keeps results local but may find none. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The message shown when the In-Store Delivery method is unavailable.
field.usage: The error text displayed to shoppers when In-Store Delivery cannot be offered for their cart. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The title shown to shoppers for the In-Store Delivery carrier.
field.usage: The heading shown for the In-Store Delivery carrier above its method at checkout. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Turns the Table Rates shipping method on or off at checkout.

values.value: Look up the rate by weight and destination.

field.usage: Exports this website's Table Rates to a CSV file for editing or backup. Operates at website scope.

field.summary: The handling fee added to the Table Rates shipping charge.
field.usage: The handling fee amount added to Table Rate shipping, applied according to Calculate Handling Fee. Can be set per website.

field.summary: How the Table Rates handling fee is calculated.
field.usage: Sets the basis for the handling fee added to Table Rate shipping — for example a fixed amount or a proportion of the rate. Works together with Handling Fee. Can be set per website.

values.value: Add a fixed handling amount.

field.summary: Uploads a CSV file of table rates for this website.
field.usage: Imports a CSV file defining the Table Rates for this website, replacing the existing rate table. Operates at website scope.

field.summary: Whether virtual products count toward the value used to look up table rates.
field.usage: When Yes, virtual products are included in the order value used for the Table Rates lookup. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The Table Rates method name shown to customers at checkout.
field.usage: The label shown next to the Table Rates price in the list of shipping methods at checkout. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Whether Table Rates is offered to all countries or only selected ones.
field.usage: Chooses whether Table Rates is available for all allowed countries or only for the countries chosen in Ship to Specific Countries. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The position of Table Rates among the shipping methods at checkout.

field.summary: The countries Table Rates is offered to when limited to specific countries.

field.summary: The message shown when Table Rates shipping is unavailable for the order.
field.usage: The error text displayed to customers when Table Rates cannot be offered for their order. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: The heading shown for the Table Rates carrier at checkout.
field.usage: The carrier title displayed above the Table Rates method at checkout. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: The UPS Access License Number used to authenticate rate and label requests to UPS.
field.usage: The UPS-issued Access License Number that authorises this store's calls to the UPS API. Stored encrypted. Can be set per website, so separate UPS accounts can serve different websites.

field.summary: Enables UPS as a shipping method offered at checkout.
field.usage: When set to Yes, UPS rates are offered to customers at checkout. Set to No to hide UPS. Can be enabled per website.

field.summary: The UPS service levels offered to customers at checkout.
field.usage: Selects which UPS shipping services (service levels) are presented to customers. Only the methods chosen here are quoted. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The UPS packaging type used when requesting rates.
field.usage: The UPS container/packaging type assumed when quoting rates. Pick the packaging that matches how you ship. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether to log UPS request and response data for troubleshooting.
field.usage: When Yes, UPS API requests and responses are written to the debug log to help diagnose rating issues. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The destination type UPS uses when calculating rates.
field.usage: Selects the kind of delivery destination UPS assumes when quoting rates, which can change the returned prices. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The UPS service level used for the free shipping option.
field.usage: The UPS service applied when an order qualifies for free shipping. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Enables a free-shipping threshold for UPS based on order subtotal.
field.usage: When enabled, orders at or above the configured subtotal qualify for free UPS shipping. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The order subtotal at which UPS shipping becomes free.
field.usage: The minimum order subtotal that qualifies for free UPS shipping. Applies only when Enable Free Shipping Threshold is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The URL of the UPS REST API endpoint.
field.usage: The endpoint URL used when UPS requests go through the REST API. Change only if directed by UPS. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The UPS gateway URL used for rate requests.
field.usage: The endpoint URL this store calls to request UPS rates. Change only if directed by UPS. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The URL of the UPS XML rate API endpoint.
field.usage: The endpoint URL used when UPS requests go through the legacy XML API. Change only if directed by UPS. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether the handling fee is applied per order or per package.
field.usage: Chooses whether the UPS handling fee is charged once per order or for each package. Can differ per website.

values.value: Apply the handling fee once per order.
Apply the handling fee to each package.

field.summary: The handling fee added to UPS shipping rates.
field.usage: The handling amount added to quoted UPS rates, interpreted as a fixed value or percentage per the Calculate Handling Fee setting. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether the handling fee is a fixed amount or a percentage.
field.usage: Chooses whether the UPS handling fee is applied as a fixed amount or as a percentage of the shipping rate. Can differ per website.

values.value: Add a fixed handling amount.
Add handling as a percentage of the rate.

field.summary: Requests tax-inclusive shipping rates from UPS, changing the quoted shipping cost.
field.usage: When Yes, UPS rate requests ask for tax-inclusive rates, so applicable taxes (sales tax, VAT) are folded into the quoted shipping price. Affects what customers see at checkout where UPS applies. Website scoped.

field.summary: Whether the UPS account runs against the live production API rather than a test environment.
field.usage: When Yes, requests go to the live UPS production environment; No targets the test environment. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The maximum package weight UPS will quote.
field.usage: The heaviest single package UPS will rate; consult UPS for the supported maximum. Orders above this may be split or return no rate. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The minimum package weight UPS will quote.
field.usage: The lightest single package UPS will rate; consult UPS for the supported minimum. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Operating mode Magento uses when calling the UPS API.
field.usage: Selects the mode for the UPS integration; per the field this governs SSL verification of your Magento server by UPS when rates and labels are requested. Set per website, so different sites can use different UPS connection settings.

field.summary: Whether to request UPS negotiated (account-specific) rates instead of published rates.
field.usage: When Yes, UPS returns the negotiated rates tied to your account rather than standard published rates. Requires a UPS account that is enabled for negotiated rates. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The UPS origin region that determines which shipping methods are available.
field.usage: The region the shipment originates from, which governs the set of UPS services that can be offered. Can differ per website.

value.id: Shipments Originating in the European Union
value.label: Shipments Originating in the European Union

field.summary: The password for the UPS account used to authenticate API requests.
field.usage: The password paired with the UPS user ID to authenticate API calls. Stored encrypted. Can be set per website.

field.summary: How packages are handed to UPS, which affects the rates returned.
field.usage: The pickup method describing how packages reach UPS (for example scheduled pickup or drop-off). The choice can change the rates UPS quotes. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether UPS is offered to all countries or only to selected ones.
field.usage: Chooses between offering UPS to all allowed countries or restricting it to the countries chosen in Ship to Specific Countries. Can differ per website.

values.value: Offer this method in every country your store already allows.
Limit this method to the specific countries you pick below.

field.summary: How package weights are packaged into UPS rate requests.
field.usage: Chooses how the cart's weight is sent to UPS when requesting rates — as a single combined request or split across packages. Affects how multi-item orders are quoted. Can differ per website.

values.value: Split the cart into equal weights and send one rate request.
Use the real package weight and send a request per package.

field.summary: Your 6-character UPS account number; required to return your negotiated rates instead of published ones.
field.usage: Your UPS shipper (account) number — 6 characters, per the note. It is required for UPS to return your contracted/negotiated rates rather than standard published rates. Set per website.

field.summary: Whether to still show UPS at checkout when it returns no applicable rates.
field.usage: When Yes, UPS remains visible at checkout even when no rate is available, showing the configured error message instead of hiding the method. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The position of UPS relative to other shipping methods at checkout.
field.usage: Controls where UPS appears in the list of shipping methods; lower numbers sort higher. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The countries UPS can ship to when limited to specific countries.
field.usage: The set of destination countries for which UPS is offered. Applies when Ship to Applicable Countries is set to specific countries. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The message shown to customers when UPS returns no available rates.
field.usage: The text displayed at checkout when UPS cannot provide a rate. Can be set per store view for localised messaging.

technical.default_value: This shipping method is currently unavailable. If you would like to ship using this shipping method, please contact us.

field.summary: The carrier name shown to customers at checkout for UPS.
field.usage: The heading customers see above the UPS shipping options at checkout. Can be set per store view, so each store can show a localised name.

field.summary: The URL of the UPS tracking REST endpoint.
field.usage: The endpoint URL used to retrieve UPS tracking information via the REST API. Change only if directed by UPS. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The URL of the UPS tracking XML endpoint.
field.usage: The endpoint URL used to retrieve UPS tracking information via the XML API. Change only if directed by UPS. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The UPS integration/account type used for rate requests.
field.usage: Selects which UPS integration this store uses when authenticating and requesting rates. Match it to the account type UPS provisioned. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The weight unit used in UPS rate requests.
field.usage: The unit of weight sent to UPS when quoting rates. Set it to match how product weights are recorded in your catalog. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The UPS user ID used to authenticate API requests.
field.usage: The UPS account user ID, paired with the password, used to authenticate API calls. Stored encrypted. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The USPS account number used with the REST API.
field.usage: The USPS account number associated with your REST API credentials. Applies only when USPS Type is REST. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: The kind of USPS account used for REST pricing.
field.usage: Selects the type of USPS account used with the REST API, which affects the pricing available. Applies only when USPS Type is REST.

field.summary: Turns the USPS shipping method on or off at checkout.
field.usage: Controls whether USPS shipping rates are offered to customers during checkout. Can be set per website.

field.summary: AES/ITN export number for international USPS shipments outside the US; applies only when the USPS REST type is selected. Per website/store.
field.usage: The Automated Export System / International Transaction Number declared on qualifying international USPS shipments for customs and export compliance. Applies only when the USPS REST API type is selected, and is relevant only for shipments leaving the US. Per website/store.

field.summary: Which USPS (XML Web Tools) shipping methods are offered to customers at checkout.
field.usage: Selects which USPS services returned by the XML Web Tools API are offered to shoppers at checkout; unselected services are hidden. Applies only when USPS Type is the XML Web Tools. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The consumer key (client ID) for the USPS REST API account.
field.usage: The OAuth consumer key issued by USPS for the REST API, used to obtain access tokens. Stored encrypted. Applies only when USPS Type is REST.

field.summary: The consumer secret (client secret) for the USPS REST API account.
field.usage: The OAuth consumer secret paired with the USPS REST consumer key. Stored encrypted; keep it confidential. Applies only when USPS Type is REST.

field.summary: The USPS package/container type reported when requesting XML rates.
field.usage: The packaging/container type reported to USPS when requesting rates, which affects eligible services and prices. Applies only when USPS Type is the XML Web Tools. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The USPS Customer Registration ID (CRID) tied to your account.
field.usage: Your USPS Customer Registration ID (CRID), identifying your business to USPS. Applies only when USPS Type is REST.

field.summary: Whether USPS request and response details are logged for troubleshooting.
field.usage: When Yes, USPS API requests and responses are written to the debug log to help diagnose rating problems. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Which USPS method is used for orders that qualify for free shipping.
field.usage: The USPS service used to fulfil orders that qualify for free shipping. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether reaching a minimum order subtotal unlocks free USPS shipping.
field.usage: Enables or disables a free-shipping threshold for USPS: when set to Enable, orders reaching the subtotal set below ship free. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The order subtotal at which USPS shipping becomes free.
field.usage: The minimum order subtotal that qualifies for free USPS shipping. Applies only when the free-shipping threshold is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The USPS REST API test endpoint URL used when not in production mode.
field.usage: The USPS REST API endpoint used for rate requests in development/test mode. Applies only when USPS Type is REST and Mode is set to development. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The USPS REST API production endpoint URL used for live rate requests.
field.usage: The USPS REST API endpoint used for rate requests in production. Applies only when USPS Type is REST and Mode is set to live/production. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The secure (HTTPS) USPS Web Tools endpoint used for requests that require it.
field.usage: The secure USPS Web Tools (XML) gateway URL, used for requests that require HTTPS. Applies only when USPS Type is the XML Web Tools. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The USPS Web Tools (XML) endpoint URL rate requests are sent to.
field.usage: The base URL of the USPS Web Tools (XML) gateway used for rate requests. Applies only when USPS Type is the XML Web Tools. Change only if USPS provides a different endpoint. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The package girth used for USPS rating when the size is Large.
field.usage: The package girth (the distance around the package) sent to USPS for rate calculation. Applies only when Size is set to Large. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the handling fee is applied once per order or to each package.
field.usage: Determines whether the handling fee is charged per order or per package. Can be set per website.

values.value: Apply the handling fee once per order.
Apply the handling fee to each package.

field.summary: The handling fee amount or percentage added to USPS rates.
field.usage: The handling fee value added to the USPS rate, interpreted as a fixed amount or a percentage according to Calculate Handling Fee. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the handling fee is a fixed amount or a percentage of the rate.
field.usage: Chooses how the handling fee is calculated — as a fixed amount or a percentage of the shipping rate. Can be set per website.

values.value: Add a fixed handling amount.
Add handling as a percentage of the rate.

field.summary: The package height used for USPS rating when the size is Large.
field.usage: The package height sent to USPS for rate calculation. Applies only when Size is set to Large. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The package length used for USPS rating when the size is Large.
field.usage: The package length sent to USPS for rate calculation. Applies only when Size is set to Large. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether packages are machinable (handled by USPS sorting machines), which affects rates.
field.usage: Declares whether shipments are machinable — able to be processed by USPS automated sorting equipment — which influences the rates returned. Applies only when USPS Type is the XML Web Tools. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The maximum weight per package before an order is split into multiple packages.
field.usage: The heaviest a single package may be; orders over this weight are divided into multiple packages for rating. Consult USPS for the maximum supported weight. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The USPS Mailer Identifier (MID) associated with your account.
field.usage: Your USPS Mailer Identifier (MID), used to identify the mailer on shipments. Applies only when USPS Type is REST.

field.summary: The Mailer Identifier (MID) used on USPS manifests.
field.usage: The Manifest MID used when generating USPS manifests. Applies only when USPS Type is REST.

field.summary: Whether the carrier connects to the USPS production or test environment.
field.usage: Switches the carrier between the USPS live/production environment and the development/test environment, which determines which gateway URL is used. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The password for the USPS Web Tools (XML) account.
field.usage: The password paired with the USPS Web Tools (XML) user ID. Stored encrypted. Applies only when USPS Type is the XML Web Tools.

field.summary: Which USPS pricing option is requested for rates.
field.usage: Selects the pricing option USPS returns for rate requests (for example retail versus commercial pricing). Applies only when USPS Type is REST.

field.summary: Which USPS (REST API) shipping methods are offered to customers at checkout.
field.usage: Selects which USPS services returned by the REST API are offered to shoppers at checkout; unselected services are hidden. Applies only when USPS Type is REST. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether USPS is offered to all allowed countries or only selected ones.
field.usage: Chooses whether USPS shipping is available for all allowed countries or only the specific countries selected below. Can be set per website.

values.value: Offer this method in every country your store already allows.
Limit this method to the specific countries you pick below.

field.summary: How items are grouped into packages when USPS rates are requested.
field.usage: Controls how items are grouped into packages for rate requests (for example a single combined request versus per-package requests). Can be set per website.

values.value: Split the cart into equal weights and send one rate request.
Use the real package weight and send a request per package.

field.summary: Whether USPS is still listed at checkout when it returns no rates.
field.usage: When Yes, the USPS carrier is shown at checkout even when it returns no applicable rates, typically with the error message. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The package size category sent to USPS; selecting Large reveals dimension fields.
field.usage: The USPS package size category. Choosing the Large size requires the width, length, height and girth values below. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The position of USPS relative to other carriers in the checkout list.
field.usage: A numeric value controlling where USPS appears among shipping carriers at checkout; lower values sort higher. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The countries USPS shipping is offered to when limited to specific countries.
field.usage: The list of destination countries that may use USPS shipping, applied when Ship to Applicable Countries is set to specific countries. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The message shown to customers when USPS rates can't be retrieved.
field.usage: The text shown to shoppers at checkout when the USPS carrier cannot return a rate. Can differ per store view.

technical.default_value: This shipping method is currently unavailable. If you would like to ship using this shipping method, please contact us.

field.summary: The carrier name shown to customers next to USPS shipping options at checkout.
field.usage: The label displayed to shoppers for this carrier's shipping methods at checkout. Can differ per store view, so each storefront can show its own wording.

field.summary: The USPS Web Tools (XML) account user ID used to authenticate rate requests.
field.usage: The user ID issued by USPS for the Web Tools (XML) API, used to authenticate requests. Stored encrypted. Applies only when USPS Type is the XML Web Tools.

field.summary: Which USPS API integration to use — the legacy XML Web Tools or the newer REST API.
field.usage: Selects the USPS API the carrier connects through: the legacy USPS Web Tools (XML) or the newer USPS REST API. The choice determines which credential and gateway fields below apply. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The package width used for USPS rating when the size is Large.
field.usage: The package width sent to USPS for rate calculation. Applies only when Size is set to Large. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The order in which the day, month and year inputs appear for date custom options.
field.usage: Sets the arrangement of the day, month and year fields for date-type custom options, to match local date conventions.

field.summary: Whether time custom options use a 12-hour or 24-hour clock.
field.usage: Chooses between a 12h (AM/PM) and a 24h time format for time-type custom options.

values.value: Show times in 12-hour AM/PM format.
Show times in 24-hour format.

field.summary: Whether date-type custom options use a JavaScript date picker.
field.usage: When Yes, date and time custom options are entered through a JavaScript calendar instead of separate dropdowns.

field.summary: Sets the from-to years offered by date custom options; use a four-digit year.
field.usage: Limits the span of years selectable in product date/time custom-option dropdowns. Use a four-digit year format for both ends, per the native note. The range can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Whether downloads are delivered inline or as a file attachment.
field.usage: Sets the HTTP Content-Disposition for downloads, choosing whether files are served inline (shown in the browser) or as an attachment (prompting a save). Can differ per website or store view.

values.value: Force downloadable files to download.
Let the browser open downloadable files in place.

field.summary: Forces account creation when the cart has downloadable items, so download links belong to an account.
field.usage: When Yes, guest checkout is blocked for carts containing downloadable products, so purchases tie to a registered account. As the native note says, guest checkout still works only for shareable downloads. Website scoped.

field.summary: The default limit on how many times a downloadable link can be downloaded.
field.usage: The default maximum number of downloads allowed per link for new downloadable products. Individual products can override this. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether download links open in a new browser window.
field.usage: When Yes, downloadable links open in a new browser window or tab instead of the current one. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The default heading shown above a downloadable product's links.
field.usage: The default title for the downloadable links section on product pages. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The order item status at which a customer's downloads become available.
field.usage: Determines when purchased downloads are released to the customer, based on the order item's status (such as Pending or Invoiced). Can be set per website.

values.value: Grant access to downloads once the order is Pending.
Grant access to downloads only after the order is Invoiced.

field.summary: The default heading shown above a downloadable product's samples.
field.usage: The default title for the samples section on downloadable product pages. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether downloadable links can be shared rather than tied to the purchasing account.
field.usage: When Yes, download links are shareable and can be accessed without signing in to the purchasing account; when No, access is restricted to that account. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Template that auto-fills a product's meta description when none is set, keeping SEO metadata consistent; use {{name}}/{{description}}.
field.usage: A mask that auto-generates the meta description for products that lack one, keeping SEO metadata consistent across the catalog. Use {{name}} and {{description}} as placeholders for the product name and description. Applies only when a product has no manual meta description. Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Template that auto-builds a product's Meta Keywords from placeholders like {{name}} and {{sku}}.
field.usage: The pattern used to auto-generate a product's Meta Keywords, built from placeholders such as {{name}} and {{sku}} (per the note). It fills the SEO meta-keywords field for products that don't have one set, saving manual entry across a catalogue. Default scope.

field.summary: Template for auto-filling a product's meta title when left blank; {{name}} inserts the product name.
field.usage: Pattern used to generate a product's Meta Title when it isn't set manually, with {{name}} standing in for the product name. Applied when products are saved, so existing products keep their current titles until re-saved.

field.summary: Template for auto-building a new product's SKU when left blank; use {{name}} for the product name. Affects only products created afterward.
field.usage: Pattern used to auto-generate a SKU when a product is saved without one, with {{name}} standing in for the product name. It only shapes SKUs of products created after the change; existing SKUs are untouched.

field.summary: Initial sort order on category listings before a shopper chooses one; an individual category can override it. Per website/store.
field.usage: The sort order category pages use by default until a shopper picks another; the options are your available sort attributes. An individual category can override this, and the default can differ per website/store view.

values.value: Default sort by the position set in the category.
Default sort by product name.
Default sort by price.

field.summary: Default sort order for category product listings; shoppers can still re-sort.
field.usage: The initial sort applied to category product lists. It only sets the default — shoppers can re-sort — and applies to category pages per the native note. Website/store scoped, so store views can differ.

values.value: Sort ascending (A–Z, low–high).
Sort descending (Z–A, high–low).

field.summary: Whether the storefront reads categories from flat (denormalized) tables.
field.usage: When Yes, category data is served from a flat table for faster reads. A legacy performance option; leave off unless a specific setup requires it.

field.summary: Whether the storefront reads products from flat (denormalized) tables.
field.usage: When Yes, product data is served from a flat table for faster reads. A legacy performance option; leave off unless a specific setup requires it.

field.summary: Default products-per-page for grid view; must be one of the allowed values.
field.usage: Default number of products shown per page in grid view. As the native note says, it must be one of the configured 'allowed values' list or it is rejected. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: The choices in the storefront per-page selector; the default per-page value must be one of these.
field.usage: Comma-separated list of options offered in the 'products per page' selector on grid category pages. The configured default per-page value must appear in this list, otherwise the selector falls back unexpectedly. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Yes adds an 'All' choice to the per-page dropdown; on big categories loading every product at once can be slow.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront's 'Show X Per Page' dropdown includes an All option (per the note). Gotcha: on large categories, letting shoppers render every product on one page is slow and easy to abuse for scraping. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: The default layout of product lists — grid, list, or a toggle between them.
field.usage: How category product lists are displayed by default: Grid Only, List Only, Grid (default) / List, or List (default) / Grid (the latter two let shoppers switch).

values.value: Show products as a grid only.
Show products as a list only.
Grid by default, with a toggle to list.
List by default, with a toggle to grid.

field.summary: Default number of products shown per page in list mode; must be one of the allowed values.
field.usage: The default products-per-page for the catalog list view. As the field note says, the value must appear in the allowed-values list configured alongside it, or it is rejected. Scoped to website/store, so each store view can default differently.

field.summary: Comma-separated page-size options shown in the category list per-page selector.
field.usage: The comma-separated list of page-size options shoppers can pick from on category list pages; each value becomes one choice in the per-page selector. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Yes remembers each visitor's per-page choice across category pages; this multiplies cached page variants and can create duplicate SEO URLs.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront remembers each visitor's chosen products-per-page setting as they browse categories. The native note's SEO and cache warnings follow from this: storing per-page variants multiplies cached page versions and creates duplicate-content URL parameters. Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Whether a tooltip preview is shown when hovering over a swatch.
field.usage: When Yes, hovering over a swatch displays a tooltip preview of the option. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether swatches appear in product listings.
field.usage: When Yes, attribute swatches are shown for products in category and search listings; when No, they are hidden there. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: How many swatches are shown per product in product listings.
field.usage: The maximum number of swatches displayed for a single product in category and search listings. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether the category filter is shown in layered navigation.
field.usage: When Yes, layered navigation includes a category filter alongside attribute filters.

field.summary: Whether the number of matching products is shown next to each filter option.
field.usage: When Yes, layered navigation shows a count of matching products beside each filter value. Can be set per store view.

field.summary: Only used with Improved price-range calculation; controls how price filters split into sub-ranges.
field.usage: Number of products that will not be divided into sub-intervals in layered-navigation price filters. Applies only when the price range calculation is set to 'Improved'. Tune it to balance filter granularity against usability. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Yes shows a price bucket as a single price instead of a range when every item in it has the same price.
field.usage: When Yes, a layered-navigation price filter bucket displays one price rather than a from–to range if all prices within it are equal (native note). Applies only with the Improved price range calculation (depends). Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: How price filter ranges are calculated — automatically or by a manual step.
field.usage: Chooses how price-filter buckets are built: automatically, or using a manual fixed step set in Default Price Navigation Step. Can be set per store view.

values.value: Build price ranges with equal spans automatically.
Build price ranges with roughly equal product counts.
Use the fixed price step you set.

field.summary: Caps how many price brackets layered navigation builds in manual mode (max 100); more means finer filters but a longer list.
field.usage: The upper limit on the number of price intervals layered navigation generates, up to 100 (per the note). More intervals give finer price filters but a longer sidebar list. Applies only when price-range calculation is set to manual. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: The fixed price interval used to build price-filter ranges.
field.usage: The price interval for each price-filter range. Applies only when Price Navigation Step Calculation is set to Manual. Can be set per store view.

field.summary: How many category levels deep the top navigation menu renders.
field.usage: The maximum category depth shown in the storefront top menu. A smaller value keeps the menu shallow on deep category trees.

field.summary: The fallback images shown for products that have no image of their own.
field.usage: Upload the placeholder images (base, small and thumbnail) used wherever a product is missing its own image.

field.summary: Global vs per-website pricing; switching to website lets each site set its own prices but needs a reindex.
field.usage: Sets whether product prices are shared globally or managed per website (which also fixes the base-currency scope). Switching to Website lets each website keep its own prices but is disruptive to reverse and requires a price reindex.

values.value: One price per product across the whole catalog.
Allow a different price per website.

field.summary: Whether a product's base video plays automatically on the product page.
field.usage: When Yes, the video marked as the product's base media starts playing automatically on the product page. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether related videos are shown when a product video ends.
field.usage: When Yes, related videos are displayed after a product video finishes playing. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether a product video restarts automatically after it finishes.
field.usage: When Yes, a product video loops, restarting automatically once it reaches the end. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The YouTube Data API key used to fetch video details when adding product videos.
field.usage: The API key the admin uses to call the YouTube Data API when retrieving metadata for product videos hosted on YouTube. Obtain it from the Google API console.

field.summary: Whether customers can sign up to be emailed when a product's price changes.
field.usage: When Yes, a price-change alert sign-up appears on product pages so customers can be emailed when the price changes; No removes it. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether customers can sign up to be emailed when an out-of-stock product is available again.
field.usage: When Yes, an in-stock alert sign-up appears on product pages so customers can be notified when the item returns to stock; No removes it. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The email address notified if the product alert cron job fails.
field.usage: The recipient address for error notifications raised when the product-alert cron job cannot complete. Leave empty to send no error email.

field.summary: Which store email identity product alert error emails are sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity for product-alert error notifications — one of the Store Email Addresses identities configured under General → Store Email Addresses.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Email template for the alert sent when the product-alert cron job (price/stock alerts) fails.
field.usage: Selects the template for the email sent to administrators when the product alerts cron run encounters an error. Choosing Default falls back to the theme's template (native note). Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: How often the scheduled job that sends product alert emails runs.
field.usage: Sets the schedule for the product-alert cron job that sends pending price and stock notifications. Choose from the available frequency options.

values.value: Run once a day.
Run once a week.
Run once a month.

field.summary: The time of day the product alert cron job runs.
field.usage: The start time (hour, minute, second) at which the product-alert cron job runs on its configured frequency.

field.summary: Which store email identity product alert emails are sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity used for product alert emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2) configured under General → Store Email Addresses. Can differ per store view.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Email template for product price-drop alert notifications.
field.usage: Selects the template used for price-alert emails sent when a watched product's price drops. Choosing Default resolves via theme fallback per the native note. Website/store scoped, so each store view can brand it.

field.summary: Email template for the 'back in stock' alert customers subscribe to; choose a custom one or keep Default.
field.usage: The template for the stock (back-in-stock) alert email sent to customers who subscribed to be notified when a product is available again. Pick a custom template to brand it, or leave Default, which follows theme fallback (per the note). Set per website or store view.

field.summary: The number of products shown in the Recently Compared block.
field.usage: The maximum number of items displayed in the Recently Compared Products block. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: How long a product stays in the Recently Compared widget, in days.
field.usage: The retention period, in days, for entries shown by the Recently Compared Products widget.

field.summary: How long a product stays in the Recently Viewed widget, in days.
field.usage: The retention period, in days, for entries shown by the Recently Viewed Products widget.

field.summary: The scope recently viewed/compared product lists are tracked across.
field.usage: Sets whether recently viewed and compared products are tracked per Website, Store, or Store View. Can be set per website.

values.value: Aggregate report data per website.
Aggregate report data per store.
Aggregate report data per store view.

field.summary: Whether recently viewed/compared products are stored server-side rather than only in the browser.
field.usage: When Yes, the recently viewed/compared lists are synchronised to backend storage, so they follow a signed-in customer across devices instead of living only in the browser.

field.summary: The number of products shown in the Recently Viewed block.
field.usage: The maximum number of items displayed in the Recently Viewed Products block. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Turns product reviews on or off on the storefront.
field.usage: Controls whether the Product Reviews feature is available on the storefront, letting shoppers read and submit reviews. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether visitors who aren't logged in can submit product reviews.
field.usage: When Yes, guests who are not signed-in customers can write product reviews; when No, only registered customers can. Applies only when Product Reviews is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Maximum number of suggestions shown in the search autocomplete dropdown.
field.usage: Caps how many suggestions the search box shows as the shopper types.

field.summary: Whether HTTP authentication is used when connecting to Elasticsearch 8.
field.usage: When Yes, a username and password are sent with requests to the Elasticsearch 8 server. Applies only when the search engine is set to Elasticsearch 8.

field.summary: The prefix added to the names of the Elasticsearch 8 indices.
field.usage: The string prepended to index names in Elasticsearch 8, letting several stores or environments share one cluster without index-name collisions. Applies only when the search engine is set to Elasticsearch 8.

field.summary: How many query terms a product must match to appear in Elasticsearch results; stricter values return fewer, more relevant hits.
field.usage: Sets Elasticsearch's minimum_should_match for catalog search: how many of the query's terms a product must contain to be returned. Stricter values give fewer, more precise results; looser ones return more but noisier matches. Applies only with the Elasticsearch 8 engine (depends).

field.summary: The password for Elasticsearch 8 HTTP authentication.
field.usage: The password used together with the user name to authenticate to the Elasticsearch 8 server. Applies only when Elasticsearch 8 is the search engine and HTTP authentication is enabled.

field.summary: The hostname or IP address of the Elasticsearch 8 server.
field.usage: The host where the Elasticsearch 8 cluster is reached. Applies only when the search engine is set to Elasticsearch 8.

field.summary: The TCP port the Elasticsearch 8 server listens on.
field.usage: The port used to connect to the Elasticsearch 8 server. Applies only when the search engine is set to Elasticsearch 8.

field.summary: How long, in seconds, to wait for the Elasticsearch 8 server before timing out.
field.usage: The connection timeout for requests to the Elasticsearch 8 server. Applies only when the search engine is set to Elasticsearch 8.

field.summary: The user name for Elasticsearch 8 HTTP authentication.
