field.usage: The account name used to authenticate to the Elasticsearch 8 server. Applies only when Elasticsearch 8 is the search engine and HTTP authentication is enabled.

field.summary: Yes maintains a dedicated product EAV index to speed reindexing; check no third-party extension relies on it before disabling.
field.usage: When Yes, Magento keeps a separate product EAV indexer, speeding up indexation. Relevant with the MySQL search engine (depends). As the native note warns, confirm no third-party extension uses this index before turning it off. Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Selects the search engine backend; falls back to the default engine when unset.
field.usage: Chooses which search engine backend powers catalog search. As the field note says, the default search engine is used when nothing is specified. Changing the engine requires the matching service to be running and a search reindex before results reflect the new backend.

values.value: Index and search with Elasticsearch 8 (deprecated).
Index and search with OpenSearch.

field.summary: How many popular search terms to cache; 0 caches all after a term's second search. Higher speeds more searches but uses more cache.
field.usage: Caps how many popular search terms are cached for faster results; 0 caches every term after its second search (per the note). A higher cap serves more searches from cache at the cost of more cache storage. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Longest search string accepted; must stay compatible with the configured search engine's limit.
field.usage: Caps the length of storefront search queries. Set it beyond what your search engine allows and searches can error, so keep the two in sync as the native note warns. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Shortest search term that returns results; must match the search engine's own minimum or results won't line up. Per website/store.
field.usage: The minimum number of characters a shopper must type before search returns results. As the native note says, it must be consistent with the configured search engine (OpenSearch/Elasticsearch); a mismatch means queries the engine would answer get rejected, or vice-versa. A very low value hurts performance. Per website/store.

field.summary: Whether to send HTTP authentication credentials when connecting to OpenSearch.
field.usage: When Yes, Magento authenticates to OpenSearch using the configured username and password. Applies only when the search engine is set to OpenSearch.

field.summary: A prefix added to OpenSearch index names for this installation.
field.usage: Prepended to the names of the catalog search indexes, letting several installations share one OpenSearch cluster without clashing. Applies only when the search engine is set to OpenSearch.

field.summary: How many query terms a document must match to be returned; stricter values narrow results.
field.usage: Passes a minimum-should-match rule to OpenSearch controlling how many of a query's terms a result must contain. Stricter settings return fewer, more precise matches; looser ones broaden recall. Applies only when the OpenSearch engine is selected. Default scope.

field.summary: The password for HTTP authentication to OpenSearch.
field.usage: The password used to authenticate to the OpenSearch server. Applies only when the engine is OpenSearch and Enable OpenSearch HTTP Auth is set to Yes.

field.summary: The hostname or IP address of the OpenSearch server used for catalog search.
field.usage: The address Magento connects to when indexing and querying catalog search. Applies only when the search engine is set to OpenSearch.

field.summary: The port on which the OpenSearch server accepts connections.
field.usage: The TCP port used to reach the OpenSearch server. Applies only when the search engine is set to OpenSearch.

field.summary: The request timeout for connections to the OpenSearch server.
field.usage: How long Magento waits for an OpenSearch request before timing out. Applies only when the search engine is set to OpenSearch.

field.summary: The username for HTTP authentication to OpenSearch.
field.usage: The user name used to authenticate to the OpenSearch server. Applies only when the engine is OpenSearch and Enable OpenSearch HTTP Auth is set to Yes.

field.summary: How many search term recommendations to show.
field.usage: The number of alternative search-term recommendations shown for a query. Applies only when search recommendations are enabled. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Whether to show the number of results next to each search recommendation.
field.usage: When Yes, each search recommendation displays how many results it would return. Applies only when search recommendations are enabled. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Suggests alternative searches for weak queries; adds query-time work that can slow the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, search result pages offer recommended alternative queries. Generating them adds processing on each search — the native note's slowdown warning — so weigh it against the extra help for shoppers. Website/store scoped, so you can enable it per store view.

field.summary: How many search suggestions to show.
field.usage: The number of search suggestions offered for a query. Applies only when search suggestions are enabled. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Adds a result count beside each search suggestion; computing a count per suggestion adds queries, which is why it can slow the storefront.
field.usage: Shows how many products match each search suggestion. Each suggestion needs its own count query, which is the load the native note warns about. Applies only when search suggestions are enabled. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Yes offers as-you-type search suggestions; each adds index queries, so weigh the speed hit on busy stores.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront search box offers suggested terms as shoppers type. The native warning reflects the cost: every keystroke can hit the search index, so on high-traffic stores or large catalogues this adds real load. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether a canonical link meta tag is added to category pages.
field.usage: When Yes, category pages emit a rel="canonical" tag pointing at the preferred URL, helping search engines avoid duplicate-content issues.

field.summary: Appended to every category URL; changing it rewrites all category URLs and can break old links.
field.usage: Suffix (e.g. .html) added to category URLs. Changing it rewrites every category URL, so existing inbound links break unless redirects are in place, and you must refresh the cache afterwards. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Yes builds category-path product URLs; No permanently deletes them with no restore.
field.usage: Yes generates URL rewrites that include the category path for products, shaping storefront URLs and their SEO. Turning it No permanently deletes those existing rewrites with no way to restore them, which can break indexed links.

field.summary: Whether a canonical link meta tag is added to product pages.
field.usage: When Yes, product pages emit a rel="canonical" tag pointing at the preferred URL (useful when a product is reachable under multiple category paths).

field.summary: Whether product URL rewrites are generated at website or store-view scope.
field.usage: Controls the scope at which product URL rewrites are created when a product is edited: per website or per store view, as the field note describes. Store-view scope yields more granular URLs per view but produces more rewrite records to maintain.

values.value: Generate product URL rewrites per website.
Generate product URL rewrites per store view.

field.summary: Suffix appended to product URLs (e.g. .html); changing it rewrites every product URL.
field.usage: The suffix added to product URLs, such as .html. Can differ per website/store view. Changing it alters every product URL and requires URL rewrites to regenerate plus a cache refresh; old URLs may 404 unless redirects exist.

field.summary: Whether accented/non-Latin characters are transliterated when building product URL keys.
field.usage: When Yes, characters like 'é' are converted to ASCII when a product's URL key is generated, producing cleaner URLs.

field.summary: Whether product URLs include their category path.
field.usage: When Yes, a product reachable under a category gets a URL that includes the category path (e.g. /gear/bags/product). Affects URL structure and canonicalisation.

field.summary: Whether a permanent (301) redirect is created when a product or category URL key changes.
field.usage: When Yes, changing a URL key leaves behind a permanent redirect from the old URL, so existing links and search rankings are preserved.

field.summary: Enables the storefront Popular Search Terms page.
field.usage: When enabled, a public page listing popular search terms is published, which can help search engines discover catalog pages.

field.summary: The character placed between parts of the page title.
field.usage: The separator (e.g. - or |) used to join segments of the HTML page title.

field.summary: Yes runs bulk inventory actions via the message queue; requires a running queue consumer.
field.usage: Yes routes admin bulk inventory actions through the message queue so large updates run in the background instead of blocking the admin screen. It needs a running queue consumer; without one the queued jobs never process.

field.summary: How many items are processed per batch in asynchronous admin bulk operations.
field.usage: Sets the number of records handled in each batch when admin bulk stock/source operations run asynchronously. Applies only when asynchronous bulk operations are enabled. Larger batches finish in fewer passes but use more memory per run.

field.summary: Sync vs async reindex of stock/source data; async offloads the work to the message queue.
field.usage: Chooses whether stock/source index updates run inline or are queued for asynchronous processing. As the field note says, async mode needs a configured queue manager (consumers running). Async keeps admin saves and imports fast by deferring the reindex off the request.

values.value: Update stock indexes immediately as changes happen.
Update stock indexes in the background via the queue.

field.summary: Whether refunding an item automatically returns its quantity to stock.
field.usage: When Yes, the Return to Stock option is ticked by default when a credit memo is created, so refunded quantities go back into inventory. Staff can still change it per credit memo.

values.value: Refunded quantities are returned to stock by default.
Refunded quantities are not returned unless chosen on the credit memo.

field.summary: Whether customers can order more than the quantity in stock.
field.usage:
Controls what happens when a shopper orders beyond available stock. Allowing backorders lets quantity fall below zero so the order is still accepted.

Changing this reprocesses the whole catalog, so it can take some time.

values.value: Orders cannot exceed available stock.
Stock may go negative; orders are accepted with no notice to the customer.

value.label: Allow Qty Below 0 and Notify Customer

values.value: Backorders are accepted and the shopper is told the item is backordered.

field.summary: Whether products must be purchased in fixed multiples.
field.usage: Turns on quantity increments, forcing shoppers to buy in multiples of the Qty Increments value below — for example, in packs of 6.

values.value: Quantities are restricted to multiples of the increment.
Any quantity may be ordered (subject to min and max).

field.summary: Master switch for whether Magento tracks inventory quantities at all.
field.usage:
When Yes, Magento tracks quantities and enforces stock status for products that use the default settings. When No, products are always treated as available and quantity is ignored.

Changing this reprocesses the whole catalog, so it can take some time.

values.value: Inventory is tracked and stock status is enforced.
Stock is not tracked; products are always purchasable.

field.summary: The largest quantity of a single product a customer may buy in one order.
field.usage: Caps how many of one product can be placed in the cart. Applies to products using the default inventory settings; a per-product value overrides it.

field.summary: The quantity at which a product is considered out of stock.
field.usage: When available stock drops to this number, the product is marked Out of Stock. A negative value — together with backorders — lets stock fall below zero while the product stays sellable.

field.summary: The smallest quantity of a product a customer must buy in one order.
field.usage: Sets the minimum quantity required to add a product to the cart. Can be set per customer group, and overridden per product.

field.summary: The stock level at or below which a product is flagged as low on admin reports.
field.usage: Sets the quantity that marks a product as low on stock for the admin Low Stock report and notifications. It does not affect whether the product can be sold.

field.summary: The multiple in which a product must be purchased when increments are enabled.
field.usage: The step size shoppers must order in — for example 6 means quantities of 6, 12, 18 and so on. Only applies when Enable Qty Increments is set to Yes.

field.summary: Whether cancelling an order can flip a product back to "In Stock".
field.usage: When an order is cancelled and its items return to stock, this decides whether a product that had dropped to Out of Stock is automatically set back to In Stock. Applies only while stock is being managed.

values.value: A cancelled order's returned quantity can move the product back to In Stock.
Stock status is left unchanged; the product stays Out of Stock until set manually.

field.summary: Whether placing an order immediately reduces a product's stock quantity.
field.usage: Controls whether Magento subtracts ordered quantities from stock the moment an order is placed. In most setups this should stay Yes so available quantity reflects open orders; set it to No only when an external system owns stock levels.

values.value: Ordered quantities are subtracted from stock when the order is placed.
Stock is left unchanged when an order is placed; quantities must be adjusted elsewhere.

field.summary: Whether the storefront shows a product's "In Stock" / "Out of Stock" availability.
field.usage: Controls whether the stock-availability label is shown to shoppers on product pages. Setting it to No hides the availability line without changing how stock is tracked.

values.value: Shoppers see the In Stock / Out of Stock label.
The availability label is hidden from the storefront.

field.summary: Yes re-checks stock on every cart load (accurate, more queries); No is faster but skips that validation.
field.usage: When Yes, cart item stock is re-validated each time the cart loads, keeping availability accurate at the cost of extra queries. When No, that pre-validation is skipped for a faster cart, but out-of-stock items may linger until checkout.

field.summary: Which message shoppers see when they request more than the available quantity.
field.usage: Chooses the wording shown when a customer tries to add more of a product than is in stock.

values.value: Tells the shopper exactly how many units are available.
Shows a generic shortage message without naming the number available.

field.summary: Whether out-of-stock products appear in category listings and search results.
field.usage:
When Yes, products with no available stock still appear in category pages, search and layered navigation. When No, they are hidden from listings but remain reachable by their direct product URL.

Changing this invalidates the catalog and search indexes, so the storefront keeps the previous behaviour until reindexing completes.

values.value: Out-of-stock products are listed and searchable.
Out-of-stock products are hidden from listings, but still reachable by direct URL.

field.summary: Quantity at or below which the storefront shows an "Only X left" message.
field.usage: Sets the low-stock quantity that triggers the Only X left urgency message on the product page. Set it to 0 to turn the message off entirely.

field.summary: Whether inventory data is auto-synced when the catalog changes.
field.usage: When Yes, inventory stock and source data is kept in step automatically as products are added to or removed from the catalog. When No, that reconciliation must be triggered manually. Global scope.

field.summary: Adds a Delete mass action to the Reservations grid, able to remove even uncompensated reservations.
field.usage: Beyond the native note: this exposes a Delete mass action on the inventory Reservations grid (gated by ACL) that drops reservations outright, unlike Clean which only clears compensated ones. It is a global setting — leave it off except for deliberate recovery, since deleting live reservations can desync salable quantity.

field.summary: Google key used to geocode and measure distances for distance-based source selection; stored encrypted. Needs Geocoding + Distance Matrix APIs.
field.usage: The Google API key distance-based source selection uses to geocode addresses and compute shipping distances to sources. Per the native note, both the Geocoding and Distance Matrix APIs must be enabled on the key, or source selection cannot rank sources. Stored encrypted.

field.summary: The travel mode Google uses to measure distance — driving, walking, or bicycling.
field.usage: Chooses the Google travel mode for distance calculation: Driving, Walking, or Bicycling. Used when the Google distance provider is selected.

field.summary: Whether sources are ranked by physical distance or by travel time.
field.usage: Chooses the metric Google returns for ranking sources: Distance (physical distance) or Time to destination (travel time). Used when the Google distance provider is selected.

field.summary: Which distance provider is used to rank sources for distance-based source selection.
field.usage: Selects the service that calculates the distance between a shipping destination and each source when the Distance Based source selection algorithm runs.

field.summary: Decides how item quantities combine when a returning customer's guest cart and saved cart overlap.
field.usage: When a logged-in customer has the same item in both their guest cart and their saved cart, this chooses how the quantities are combined. The options set the merge rule — such as which quantity wins or whether they add together. Default scope.

value.label: Guest Priority – Override with guest cart quantity

values.value: When carts merge at login, keep the guest cart's quantities.

value.label: Customer Priority – Override with customer cart quantity

values.value: When carts merge at login, keep the saved customer cart's quantities.

value.label: Merge Quantities – Merge quantities of customer and guest cart

values.value: When carts merge at login, add the quantities together.

field.summary: Whether the cart shows the chosen variation's image or the configurable parent product's image.
field.usage: Controls which image appears in the shopping cart for a configurable product line: the image of the specific variation the customer selected, or the parent product's image. Can be set per website or store view.

values.value: Use each product's own thumbnail in the cart.
Use the parent (configurable/grouped) product's thumbnail.

field.summary: Whether cross-sell product suggestions are shown on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: Controls the display of cross-sell ("you might also like") products on the cart page.

field.summary: How many days an inactive cart (quote) is kept before it is cleared.
field.usage: The lifetime, in days, of an abandoned shopping cart. After this period the quote is eligible to be removed by the clean-up process.

field.summary: Whether an "empty cart" button is shown on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: When Yes, customers get a button to clear the whole cart in one action.

field.summary: Which image represents a grouped product's items in the cart — the grouped parent's or each associated product's own.
field.usage: Chooses whether the shopping cart shows the grouped (parent) product's image or each associated product's own image for items added as part of a grouped product. Can be set per store view.

values.value: Use each product's own thumbnail in the cart.
Use the parent (configurable/grouped) product's thumbnail.

field.summary: Whether the cart link counts distinct items or total item quantity.
field.usage: Chooses what the header cart summary counts: the number of distinct items in the cart, or the total quantity across all items.

value.label: Display number of items in cart

values.value: Show the count of line items in the mini-cart.
Show the total quantity of units in the mini-cart.

field.summary: Number of cart line items shown per page before pagination appears.
field.usage: How many items the shopping cart lists on one page; once the cart holds more, a pager is shown.

field.summary: Whether adding a product sends the shopper straight to the cart or leaves them on the page.
field.usage: When Yes, adding a product redirects to the shopping cart page. When No, the shopper stays where they are (typically with a mini-cart update).

field.summary: Whether the billing address is collected on the payment step or on its own checkout page.
field.usage: Chooses where the billing address is asked for: on the Payment Method step, or on a separate Payment Page.

values.value: Collect the billing address on the payment step.
Collect the billing address on its own page.

field.summary: Turns the Terms and Conditions step on at checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, the configured Terms and Conditions are shown at checkout and must be accepted before an order can be placed. Can be set per store view.

field.summary: Lets guests check if an email already has an account — convenient, but it discloses account existence.
field.usage: Scoped per website and store view, so the email lookup can be turned on only where you want it. Weigh the smoother guest checkout against revealing to unauthenticated users whether an email is already registered.

field.summary: Lets shoppers place an order without creating or signing into an account.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can check out as a guest. When No, they must register or sign in before they can place an order.

field.summary: How many line items the order summary lists before the rest are collapsed.
field.usage: The number of items shown in the checkout order summary; any beyond this are hidden behind a toggle to keep the summary short.

field.summary: Turns the one-page checkout flow on or off for the storefront.
field.usage: Controls whether customers check out through Magento's single-page checkout. Set to No to disable it (for example when a custom checkout replaces it).

field.summary: How copies of the payment-failed email are sent — blind copy or a separate email.
field.usage: Chooses how additional recipients receive the payment-failure notice: as a Bcc on the original email, or as a Separate Email.

values.value: Send one email and blind-copy the extra recipients.
Send each recipient a separate copy of the email.

field.summary: Extra recipients who get a copy of payment-failed emails; handy for monitoring failed checkouts.
field.usage: Additional addresses copied on the payment-failed notification email, separated by commas. Useful for routing failed-payment alerts to staff or a monitoring inbox. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Which store email identity the "payment failed" notification is sent from.
field.usage: The sender identity for payment-failure emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2).

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Which store email identity receives the "payment failed" notification.
field.usage: The internal recipient of payment-failure emails, chosen from the configured Store Email Addresses identities.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Email template for the notice sent to customers when a checkout payment attempt fails.
field.usage: Selects the email template used to notify customers that a payment attempt failed during checkout. Choosing Default falls back to the theme's template (native note); pick a custom template to override it. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: How many of the most recent items the mini-cart shows before it scrolls.
field.usage: The number of items visible in the mini-cart before its list becomes scrollable.

field.summary: Whether the mini-cart dropdown is shown in the page header.
field.usage: Controls the header mini-cart. Set to No to hide the dropdown cart preview.

field.summary: Maximum number of items the mini-cart will list.
field.usage: An upper bound on how many items the mini-cart renders, regardless of cart size, to keep the dropdown manageable.

field.summary: Number of columns in new Page Builder column layouts; changing it affects newly added content only, not existing pages.
field.usage: The default number of columns a new Page Builder column container offers. Raising or lowering it changes the grid for content created afterward; existing pages keep the grid they were built with.

field.summary: Upper limit on the number of columns a Page Builder column layout can hold.
field.usage: Sets the maximum grid size, which caps how many columns editors can add to a Page Builder row. Raising it allows denser layouts; lowering it constrains content authors. Default scope.

field.summary: Previews Page Builder content on product and category edit pages; No can improve admin performance.
field.usage: Renders a live Page Builder preview on product and category edit pages. Applies only when Page Builder is enabled. As the native note says, setting No can speed up the admin when several attributes are Page Builder-editable, at the cost of the inline preview.

field.summary: Turning Page Builder off reverts content editing to the legacy editor, where existing PB content may not render.
field.usage: When Yes, Page Builder's layout tools are available for CMS content and as a product-attribute input type. Turning it off reverts editing to the legacy WYSIWYG, where content already built in Page Builder may not display correctly.

field.summary: Google Maps API key enabling Page Builder's Map content type; maps won't render without it.
field.usage: The Google Maps API key that authorizes Page Builder's Map content type to render maps; without a valid key, maps do not display. Usage is billed by Google, so restrict the key to your own domains.

field.summary: Custom Google Maps style JSON that restyles the Page Builder Map content type.
field.usage: Holds the Google Maps style JSON that, as the field note says, changes the look and feel of the Map content type in Page Builder. Leave it empty for the default map appearance; paste a valid style array to recolor or simplify the map.

field.summary: Dropbox app credentials (key/secret/refresh token) that let Page Builder sync templates to and from Dropbox; stored serialized.
field.usage: Holds the Dropbox App key, secret and refresh token Page Builder uses to import/export templates from a Dropbox repository. The native note explains how to generate the refresh token; without valid credentials the sync won't connect. Applies only when the feature is enabled (depends). Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Turns Page Builder template import and export on or off.
field.usage: When set to Yes, the import and export actions for Page Builder templates are available in the admin, letting you move templates between stores.

field.summary: Yes syncs remote Page Builder templates from Dropbox on a schedule instead of on demand; suited to large libraries.
field.usage: When Yes, remote Page Builder templates are pulled from Dropbox by cron rather than fetched manually — recommended for large remote libraries. It requires the pbTemplateImport consumer in env.php, and re-saving this config before creating new credentials (per the note). Default scope.

field.summary: Selects which WYSIWYG editor adapter is used for content fields.
field.usage: Selects the WYSIWYG editor adapter used for rich-text content fields. Relates to the Enable WYSIWYG Editor setting. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether and how the WYSIWYG rich-text editor is available for content fields.
field.usage: Controls whether the WYSIWYG rich-text editor is available for content fields and how it is presented. Can be set per website or store view.

values.value: Editor is on by default and can be toggled off.
Editor is off by default but can be toggled on.
Editor is turned off completely.

field.summary: Yes hardcodes media URLs (break if base URL changes); No keeps dynamic references.
field.usage: Yes inserts media as absolute static URLs; because they are hardcoded they break if you later change the base URL. No stores dynamic references that follow the base URL. Applies only when the WYSIWYG editor is disabled.

field.summary: Turns the storefront Contact Us page and form on or off.
field.usage: Controls whether the Contact Us page and its /contact form are available on the storefront. Set to No to remove the page entirely. Can be set per website or store view, so the form can be live on one store and hidden on another.

field.summary: Template for Contact Us form emails; Default follows theme fallback, custom overrides it.
field.usage: The email template used for messages sent from the Contact Us form. Default follows theme fallback; pick a custom template to override it. Applies only when Contact Us is enabled, and can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The email address that receives messages submitted through the Contact Us form.
field.usage: The inbox that Contact Us submissions are delivered to. Applies only when Enable Contact Us is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view, so each store can route enquiries to its own team.

field.summary: Which store email identity the Contact Us notification is sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity used for the Contact Us notification — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2), configured under Stores → Configuration → General → Store Email Addresses. Applies only when Enable Contact Us is Yes.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Where CSP violation reports from admin pages are sent; the fallback for pages without their own URI.
field.usage: Endpoint that receives CSP violation reports for admin pages (the fallback for any admin page without its own URI). Collecting reports lets you tune the policy and spot blocked resources before switching admin CSP from report-only to enforced. Can differ per scope.

field.summary: URL that CSP violation reports for admin order creation are sent to; blank uses the default.
field.usage: Where the browser posts Content-Security-Policy violation reports for the admin Create Order page. Leave empty to use the admin area's default report URI per the native note. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Where CSP violation reports from one-page checkout are sent; falls back to the storefront default.
field.usage: Endpoint that receives Content-Security-Policy violation reports for the one-page checkout. If empty, the storefront default report URI is used. Lets you monitor blocked scripts on checkout without enforcing the policy. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Where browsers send CSP violation reports; use it in report-only mode before enforcing a stricter policy.
field.usage: URI that browsers POST CSP violation reports to, for storefront pages without their own report URI. Point it at a collector and run report-only mode first to see what a stricter policy would block before you enforce it. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: The API key used to authenticate with the Currency Converter API service.
field.usage: The credential for the Currency Converter API rate provider. Stored encrypted.

field.summary: How many seconds to wait for the Currency Converter API service before timing out.
field.usage: The connection timeout, in seconds, for currency rate requests to the Currency Converter API service.

field.summary: API key for the legacy Fixer.io currency feed; stored encrypted.
field.usage: The key for fetching exchange rates from Fixer.io. As the field note says, use this only for keys generated at Fixer.io directly; keys from ApiLayer belong in the separate Fixer-via-APILayer field. It is stored encrypted at rest.

field.summary: The API key used to authenticate with the Fixer (APILayer) exchange-rate service.
field.usage: The credential for the Fixer API (APILayer) currency rate provider. Stored encrypted.

field.summary: How many seconds to wait for the Fixer (APILayer) rate service before timing out.
field.usage: The connection timeout, in seconds, for currency rate requests to the Fixer API (APILayer) service.

field.summary: How many seconds to wait for the legacy Fixer.io rate service before timing out.
field.usage: The connection timeout, in seconds, for currency rate requests to the legacy Fixer.io service.

field.summary: Whether exchange rates are imported automatically on a schedule.
field.usage: When Yes, currency rates are fetched automatically from the configured service on the chosen frequency. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The email address notified when a scheduled currency rate import fails.
field.usage: The recipient for failure notifications from the scheduled rate import. Applies only when scheduled import is Enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Which store email identity sends the scheduled-import failure notification.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity for rate-import failure emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2). Applies only when scheduled import is Enabled. Can differ per website.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Template for the alert sent when a scheduled currency-rate import fails; applies only when scheduled import is enabled. Per website.
field.usage: The email template used to notify staff when the scheduled currency-rate import errors out. Applies only when scheduled import is enabled; 'Default' resolves through theme fallback. Scoped per website.

field.summary: How often the scheduled currency rate import runs.
field.usage: The cron frequency for the automatic rate import: Daily, Weekly, or Monthly. Applies only when scheduled import is Enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

values.value: Run once a day.
Run once a week.
Run once a month.

field.summary: Which exchange-rate provider the scheduled import pulls rates from.
field.usage: Selects the rate service used by the scheduled import (the configured currency import providers). Applies only when scheduled import is Enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

values.value: Import rates from Fixer.io (legacy endpoint).
Import rates from Fixer via APILayer.
Import rates from Currency Converter API.

field.summary: The time of day the scheduled currency rate import runs.
field.usage: The start time (hour, minute, second) for the automatic rate import. Applies only when scheduled import is Enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The currencies shoppers can switch between on the storefront.
field.usage: The set of currencies made available on the storefront; the Default Display Currency must be one of them. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Currency prices are stored and payments charged in; changing it needs prices and rates rechecked.
field.usage: The currency all product prices are stored in and every online payment is charged in; its scope follows Catalog Price Scope. Changing it does not reconvert stored prices, so review currency rates and prices afterwards. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The currency the storefront displays prices in by default.
field.usage: The base display currency shown to shoppers. It must be one of the Allowed Currencies. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Template for the email confirming a customer changed their email and password; a security notification.
field.usage: Selects the template for the notification sent when a customer changes their email and password — a security alert for the account owner. A custom template overrides the theme default. Set per website/store for branding.

field.summary: Email template for the security notice sent when a customer changes their account email address.
field.usage: Selects the email template used to notify a customer that their account email address was changed — a security alert about the change. Choosing Default falls back to the theme's template (native note). Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Whether customers must re-confirm their email address after changing it.
field.usage: When Yes, a customer who changes their account email must confirm the new address before it takes effect. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether the applied customer group is exposed via the GraphQL customer query.
field.usage: When No, the applied customer group is withheld from the GraphQL customer query. Set No to avoid exposing segmentation or pricing-tier information to headless/front-end clients; Yes returns it. Global scope.

field.summary: Whether a customer account is shared across all stores or kept separate per website.
field.usage: Sets account scope: Global lets a customer sign in on every website with one account; Per Website keeps accounts isolated, so the same email can register independently on each website.

field.summary: Whether Company is hidden, optional, or required on address forms.
field.usage: Controls the Company field: No hides it, Optional shows it without requiring it, Required makes it mandatory. Applies to address forms. Can differ per website.

values.value: Show the field but let shoppers leave it blank.
Show the field and require it to be filled in.

field.summary: Whether Date of Birth is hidden, optional, or required on registration and address forms.
field.usage: Controls the Date of Birth field: No hides it, Optional shows it without requiring it, Required makes it mandatory. Applies to the registration and address forms. Can differ per website.

values.value: Show the field but let shoppers leave it blank.
Show the field and require it to be filled in.

field.summary: Whether Fax is hidden, optional, or required on address forms.
field.usage: Controls the Fax field: No hides it, Optional shows it without requiring it, Required makes it mandatory. Applies to address forms. Can differ per website.

values.value: Show the field but let shoppers leave it blank.
Show the field and require it to be filled in.

field.summary: Whether Gender is hidden, optional, or required on registration and address forms.
field.usage: Controls the Gender field: No hides it, Optional shows it without requiring it, Required makes it mandatory. Applies to the registration and address forms. Can differ per website.

values.value: Show the field but let shoppers leave it blank.
Show the field and require it to be filled in.

field.summary: Shows the middle-name/initial field on customer name and address forms; it stays optional.
field.usage: Controls whether the middle name (initial) field appears on customer and address forms. Even when shown it is never required, per the native note. Website scoped, so store groups can collect it differently.

field.summary: Semicolon-separated values for the name-prefix dropdown (e.g. Mr;Mrs); leave empty to make it a free-text field. Per website.
field.usage: Defines the choices in the customer name-prefix control. Enter semicolon-separated values (e.g. Mr;Mrs;Dr) to present a dropdown, or leave it blank to let customers type a prefix freely. Scoped per website.

field.summary: Whether the name-prefix field is hidden, optional, or required on forms; can differ per website.
field.usage: Controls whether the prefix field (the title before a name, as the field note explains) is hidden, shown as optional, or made required on customer name and address forms. Scoped to website, so it can differ per website.

values.value: Show the field but let shoppers leave it blank.
Show the field and require it to be filled in.

field.summary: Number of street input lines on address forms (1-4); more suits longer addresses.
field.usage: How many street address input lines appear on customer address forms (valid range 1-4). More lines suit longer or structured addresses. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Preset options for the name-suffix dropdown (e.g. Jr., Sr.); semicolon-separated. Leave empty for a free-text field.
field.usage: Defines the selectable values for the customer name-suffix dropdown. Enter options separated by semicolons (native note); leaving it empty turns the suffix into an open text field instead of a dropdown. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether the name Suffix field (Jr., Sr., etc.) is hidden, optional, or required on storefront forms.
field.usage: Controls whether the name Suffix field (Jr., Sr., and the like, per the note) appears on storefront name and address forms, and if shown whether it is optional or required. Set per website.

values.value: Show the field but let shoppers leave it blank.
Show the field and require it to be filled in.

field.summary: Whether the Tax/VAT Number is hidden, optional, or required on registration and address forms.
field.usage: Controls the Tax/VAT Number field: No hides it, Optional shows it without requiring it, Required makes it mandatory. Applies to the registration and address forms. Can differ per website.

values.value: Show the field but let shoppers leave it blank.
Show the field and require it to be filled in.

field.summary: Whether Telephone is hidden, optional, or required on address forms.
field.usage: Controls the Telephone field: No hides it, Optional shows it without requiring it, Required makes it mandatory. Applies to address forms. Can differ per website.

values.value: Show the field but let shoppers leave it blank.
Show the field and require it to be filled in.

field.summary: HTML layout used to render customer addresses; only a small set of tags is allowed.
field.usage: Defines the HTML template for rendering customer addresses across the storefront and documents. Only the inline tags listed in the native note are permitted; others are stripped. Can differ per website/store view for locale-specific formats.

field.summary: The template that controls how an address is formatted on a single line.
field.usage: The formatting template applied when an address is rendered inline on one line. Can differ per website or store view.

technical.default_value: {{depend prefix}}{{var prefix}} {{/depend}}{{var firstname}} {{depend middlename}}{{var middlename}} {{/depend}}{{var lastname}}{{depend suffix}} {{var suffix}}{{/depend}}, {{var street}}, {{var city}}, {{var region}} {{var postcode}}, {{var country}}

field.summary: The template that controls how addresses are formatted in generated PDF documents.
field.usage: The formatting template applied to addresses printed in PDF documents such as invoices and shipments. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The template that controls how addresses are formatted as plain text.
field.usage: The formatting template applied when an address is rendered as a text block. Edit the variables and layout to change how addresses appear. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether storefront CAPTCHA answers must match letter case.
field.usage: When Yes, the entered CAPTCHA text must match the case of the displayed characters. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA on Storefront is Yes. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Turns the built-in image CAPTCHA on or off for storefront forms.
field.usage: When Yes, the legacy image CAPTCHA is required on the selected storefront forms; No disables it. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Failed logins allowed before the storefront CAPTCHA appears; 0 shows it on every attempt.
field.usage: How many unsuccessful customer logins are permitted before CAPTCHA is required. Per the native note, 0 keeps CAPTCHA always on. Applies only when CAPTCHA is enabled with mode 'after a number of failed attempts'. Website scoped.

field.summary: The font used to render the storefront CAPTCHA image.
field.usage: Selects which configured font the CAPTCHA characters are drawn with. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA on Storefront is Yes. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Chooses which storefront forms show the CAPTCHA; applies only when storefront CAPTCHA is enabled. More forms means more login/checkout friction.
field.usage: Selects which storefront forms present a CAPTCHA. Applies only when storefront CAPTCHA is enabled, and (per the native note) the Create-user and Forgot-password forms are always protected once chosen. Guarding more forms blocks more bots but adds friction for real users. Scoped per website.

field.summary: How many characters the CAPTCHA shows (max 8, ranges like 3-5 allowed); more deters bots but is harder for people.
field.usage: Number of characters in the CAPTCHA challenge — up to 8, or a range like 3-5 (per the note). More characters make automated solving harder but also raise the chance a genuine customer mistypes. Applies only when CAPTCHA is enabled. Set per website.

field.summary: When the storefront CAPTCHA is shown — e.g. always or after failed attempts.
field.usage: Chooses when a CAPTCHA is required, such as always or only after a number of failed attempts. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA on Storefront is Yes. Can be set per website.

values.value: Always show the CAPTCHA.

value.label: After number of attempts to login

values.value: Show the CAPTCHA only after a number of failed attempts.

field.summary: The pool of characters CAPTCHA images are drawn from; a clearer pool improves customer success (letters/numbers only, no spaces).
field.usage: Defines the character pool CAPTCHA images are built from. The native note allows only letters and digits (no spaces) and warns that look-alike characters (i, l, 1) hurt recognition — a clear pool is easier for customers to read. Applies only when CAPTCHA is enabled; can differ per website.

field.summary: How many minutes a displayed storefront CAPTCHA stays valid before expiring.
field.usage: The lifetime, in minutes, of a displayed CAPTCHA before a new one must be generated. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA on Storefront is Yes. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether new accounts are automatically placed in a customer group based on VAT ID validation.
field.usage: When Yes, new accounts are assigned to a customer group according to their VAT ID validation result, using the group settings below. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether new customers must confirm their email address before the account becomes active.
field.usage: When Yes, newly registered customers receive a confirmation email and must verify their address before they can sign in. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The customer group assigned to newly created accounts.
field.usage: The default customer group new accounts are placed in, chosen from the store's configured customer groups. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Email template for the account-confirmation link message sent to new customers.
field.usage: Selects which transactional template sends the account confirmation link to new customers. Choosing Default resolves via theme fallback per the native note. Website/store scoped, so each store view can use its own branded template.

field.summary: Which email template greets a customer after they confirm their new account, in place of the default welcome mail.
field.usage: Selects the email template sent once a customer confirms their newly created account, replacing the default welcome email (per the note). Choose a custom template to brand that message, or leave Default to follow theme fallback. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Default email domain used by the Create New Account flow for this store.
field.usage: Provides a default email domain for the new-account creation flow. Website/store scoped, so it can differ per store view.

field.summary: Which store email identity sends the new-account welcome email.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity for the welcome email — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2), set under General → Store Email Addresses. Can differ per website or store view.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Welcome email for accounts created without a password (admin/API); pick a template with the set-password link. Per website/store.
field.usage: Used instead of the standard welcome email when an account is created with no password, typically admin- or API-created customers. Choose a template that includes the create-password link so the customer can finish setup; 'Default' resolves via theme fallback. Per website/store.

field.summary: When Yes, an email is mandatory when an admin creates an order for a new customer; No lets the order proceed without one. Per website/store.
field.usage: Controls whether the email field is required when an admin creates an order for a new customer. Yes forces capture of an email (needed for order emails and account linkage); No lets staff place the order without one. Settable per website/store.

field.summary: Template for the welcome email sent to new customers; can differ per store view.
field.usage: The email template used for the welcome message when a customer creates an account. As the field note says, Default resolves through theme fallback. Scoped to website/store, so each store view can send its own branded welcome.

field.summary: Whether new accounts receive a human-friendly customer ID instead of the raw entity ID.
field.usage: When Yes, new customer accounts are assigned a human-friendly identifier rather than the internal sequential database ID.

field.summary: Which address — billing or shipping — is used to validate the VAT ID for group assignment.
field.usage: Chooses whether the Billing Address or Shipping Address drives VAT ID validation and tax calculation. Applies only when Enable Automatic Assignment to Customer Group is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Yes shows a VAT number field on storefront account/address forms; needed for VAT validation.
field.usage: Yes adds a VAT number field to the storefront account and address forms so customers can supply it, which is needed for VAT validation and B2B pricing. Can be set per website, so only some sites show it.

field.summary: The default value of each customer's flag that disables automatic VAT-based group changes.
field.usage: Sets the initial value of the per-customer Disable Automatic Group Changes Based on VAT ID flag. When Yes, VAT-based group reassignment is turned off by default for new customers.

field.summary: The customer group assigned when a customer's VAT ID is valid and domestic.
field.usage: The group a customer is moved to when VAT ID validation returns a valid, domestic result. Applies only when Enable Automatic Assignment to Customer Group is Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The customer group assigned when VAT ID validation cannot be completed.
field.usage: The group a customer is moved to when VAT ID validation fails to complete (for example a service error). Applies only when Enable Automatic Assignment to Customer Group is Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The customer group assigned when a customer's VAT ID is a valid intra-union (EU) number.
field.usage: The group a customer is moved to when VAT ID validation returns a valid intra-union result. Applies only when Enable Automatic Assignment to Customer Group is Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The customer group assigned when a customer's VAT ID is invalid.
field.usage: The group a customer is moved to when VAT ID validation returns an invalid result. Applies only when Enable Automatic Assignment to Customer Group is Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether the customer's VAT ID is re-validated on every order rather than only at account creation.
field.usage: When Yes, the VAT ID is re-checked and the group re-evaluated on each transaction, not just when the account is created. Applies only when Enable Automatic Assignment to Customer Group is Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Minutes a visitor counts as online in the report; empty uses the 15-minute default.
field.usage: The number of minutes a visitor keeps counting as active in the Now Online report after their last request; leave empty for the 15-minute default. A larger value reports more concurrent visitors.

field.summary: How long, in minutes, a visitor counts as online in the Online Customers grid.
field.usage: The window, in minutes as the field note says, during which a customer is still considered online after their last activity. A longer value keeps more people listed in the Online Customers grid; a shorter one trims it to recent activity only.

field.summary: Whether browsers may autocomplete the storefront login and forgot-password forms.
field.usage: When Yes, the login and forgot-password forms allow browser autocomplete of entered values. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Which store email identity sends password reset and change emails.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity for password-reset emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2). Can differ per website or store view.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Email template sent when a customer requests a password reset.
field.usage: Selects the email template for the message sent when a customer uses Forgot Password to request a reset link. Choosing Default falls back to the theme's template (native note). Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Failed customer logins before the account is locked; 0 disables locking entirely.
field.usage: Number of consecutive failed logins before a customer account is locked out. Setting 0 disables lockout completely per the native note — a convenience-versus-security tradeoff. Works together with the lockout-time setting that controls how long the lock lasts.

field.summary: Minutes a customer account stays locked after too many failed logins before it auto-unlocks.
field.usage: How long (in minutes) a customer account remains locked after exceeding the failed-login limit, after which it unlocks automatically (per the note). Longer periods slow brute-force attempts but also keep genuine locked-out customers waiting. Default scope.

field.summary: Caps customer password-reset requests per hour; 0 disables the limit. Applies under the matching protection mode.
field.usage: Limits how many password-reset requests a customer can make per hour, with 0 disabling the limit as the field note says. It applies only under the corresponding password-reset protection mode; raising it eases legitimate retries but weakens brute-force protection.

field.summary: Minutes a customer must wait between password-reset requests, to curb abuse; 0 disables the throttle. Applies under a specific reset-protection type.
field.usage: Throttles how often a customer can request a password reset, limiting reset-flooding abuse; 0 turns the delay off. It takes effect only under the matching Password Reset Protection Type setting. Can be set per website/store.

field.summary: Minimum characters for customer passwords; raising it affects only new or changed passwords, not existing ones.
field.usage: Sets the shortest allowed customer password (a number 1 or greater). Increasing it strengthens security but applies only when passwords are created or changed; existing passwords keep working until the customer next resets.

field.summary: How storefront password-reset requests are rate-limited — by IP, email, both, or not at all.
field.usage: Limits storefront customer forgot-password requests by By IP and Email, By IP, By Email, or None, to throttle abuse. Can differ per store view.

values.value: Rate-limit password resets by both IP address and email.
Rate-limit password resets by IP address.
Rate-limit password resets by email address.
Do not rate-limit password resets.

field.summary: Which template the password-reminder email uses; pick a custom one to override the default.
field.usage: Selects the email template for the password-reminder message. Choosing a custom template overrides the theme default, which is used when 'Default' is selected. Set per website/store for store-specific branding.

field.summary: How many distinct character classes a customer password must include; higher is stricter.
field.usage: The number of different character classes a customer password must contain, drawn from the four the field note lists (lowercase, uppercase, digits, special). Raising it forces more varied passwords and rejects weaker ones at registration and password change.

field.summary: Hours a password-recovery link stays valid; shorter is safer, longer is more forgiving.
field.usage: How many hours a password-recovery link stays valid (enter 1 or more). A shorter window is more secure but the link may expire before the customer uses it; a longer window is more forgiving but widens exposure if the email is intercepted.

field.summary: Email template for the customer password-reset message.
field.usage: The email template used for the customer password-reset message. As the native note says, Default follows theme fallback. Can differ per website/store view so each storefront can use its own branding.

field.summary: Yes always sends customers to the dashboard after login; No keeps them on the current page.
field.usage: When Yes, customers go to their account dashboard immediately after logging in. When No, they stay on the current page, which keeps cart and checkout flows uninterrupted. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Yes also caches custom EAV attributes, not just system ones; speeds loads but needs a cache flush after attribute changes.
field.usage: By default only system EAV attributes are cached (per the note); setting Yes also caches user-defined attributes, speeding attribute loading. Trade-off: after creating or editing custom attributes you may need to flush the cache for changes to show. Default scope.

field.summary: Combines CSS files into fewer requests to speed up page loads.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront's CSS files are merged into fewer files to reduce HTTP requests. A production performance option. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Combines and shrinks CSS to cut file size and requests; ignored in developer mode.
field.usage: Minifies storefront CSS to reduce file size and speed page loads. As the native note says, it is skipped in developer mode. Can differ per website/store view, and changes take effect after static content is redeployed and caches are flushed.

field.summary: Yes inlines critical CSS and loads the rest asynchronously to speed first render; needs a theme critical.css.
field.usage: When Yes, critical CSS is inlined and the remaining stylesheets load asynchronously, improving first render. As the field note warns, your theme must provide a critical.css file, or styling will be incomplete until the async CSS arrives.

field.summary: Shows the template file path of each block on Admin pages for debugging.
field.usage: When Yes, Admin pages display the path of the .phtml template rendering each block. A development aid; keep No in production.

field.summary: Adds each block's PHP class name alongside the template path hints.
field.usage: When Yes, the template path hints also show the PHP block class that renders each template. Only meaningful while template path hints are enabled. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Secret token added to the URL to switch storefront template hints on; applies only when hints-by-parameter is enabled.
field.usage: The token you append as ?templatehints=<value> to reveal template hints on the storefront. It applies only when storefront template hints and the show-with-parameter option are both enabled, letting developers toggle hints without exposing them to every visitor. Scoped per store view.

field.summary: Shows the template file path of each block on storefront pages for debugging.
field.usage: When Yes, storefront pages are overlaid with the path of the .phtml template rendering each block, to help locate markup. A development aid; keep No in production. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Yes lets developers toggle storefront template hints via a URL parameter instead of for all visitors.
field.usage: With Yes, developers can switch storefront template path hints on per request by adding the URL parameter, instead of showing them to every visitor. Applies only when storefront template hints are enabled, and can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Chooses server- vs client-side style compilation during development; only meaningful outside production mode.
field.usage: Selects how frontend styles are built during development, server-side compilation versus client-side compilation in the browser. As the native note says, it does nothing in production mode where static assets are pre-deployed; it only shapes the workflow in default/developer mode.

values.value: Compile LESS in the browser — convenient for development.
Compile LESS on the server — correct for production.

field.summary: Whether sales grid data is re-indexed asynchronously in the background.
field.usage: When Enabled, updates to the order, invoice, shipment and credit memo grids are indexed asynchronously by cron rather than on each save, which improves save performance on busy stores. Options are Enable and Disable.

field.summary: Picks the imaging library for catalog images; flush Catalog Images cache or old renders persist.
field.usage: Selects the PHP imaging library used to resize and process catalog images, which affects image quality and generation speed. Already-processed images stay cached, so the storefront keeps serving the old renders until you flush the Catalog Images cache.

field.summary: Yes defers non-critical head scripts to speed first render, but order-dependent inline scripts can break.
field.usage: When Yes, non-critical scripts in the head get a defer attribute so they no longer block page parsing, improving initial render. Those scripts then run later and in a different order, which can break inline code that expects them immediately. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Bundles JavaScript modules together to reduce the number of requests.
field.usage: When Yes, JavaScript is bundled for the storefront to cut request count. A production performance option. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Combines JavaScript files into fewer requests to speed up page loads.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront's JavaScript files are merged into fewer files to reduce HTTP requests. A production performance option. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Yes strips whitespace from JS to shrink downloads and speed the storefront; No serves it unminified. Ignored in developer mode.
field.usage: When Yes, JavaScript files are minified to cut payload size and speed page loads; No serves them unminified for easier debugging. As the native note says, minification is skipped in developer mode, so the effect shows only in default/production mode. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Whether JavaScript is output at the bottom of the page instead of in the head.
field.usage: When Yes, <script> tags are moved to the end of the HTML body so page content can render before scripts load, which can improve perceived load time. Applies globally (default scope).

field.summary: Browser sessionStorage key under which captured client-side JS errors are stored, so developers can read them from the console.
field.usage: Names the browser sessionStorage key where the storefront stashes collected JavaScript errors. Developers read that key in the browser console to retrieve the logged errors when debugging client-side issues.

field.summary: Yes records JS errors in the browser's session storage for test/diagnostic reporting.
field.usage: When Yes, JavaScript errors are captured into the browser's session storage. As the field note says, functional tests can read these for extended reporting; it is a diagnostic aid rather than a storefront feature.

field.summary: How JS string translations are delivered to the browser; changing it requires redeploying static files or storefront JS text breaks.
field.usage: Chooses the mechanism for delivering JavaScript translations to the storefront (for example a translation dictionary versus embedded strings). As the native note warns, switching strategy requires maintenance mode and a static-content redeploy, or client-side translated text will break.

values.value: Translate JavaScript strings on the storefront from a dictionary file.
Embed translations at render time on the server side.

field.summary: Limits developer features (like template hints) to these IPs; empty means no IP restriction.
field.usage: Restricts developer client features to a comma-separated IP allowlist. Leave empty to allow any location per the native note; set it to expose debugging tools only to your own addresses. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Appends a version to static asset URLs so browsers fetch fresh files after a deploy.
field.usage: When Yes, static files are served with a signature/version in their URL, forcing clients to reload updated assets after each deployment instead of serving stale cached copies.

field.summary: Lets themes load templates through symlinks (handy for linked local packages); on production it's an escape-the-theme-dir security risk.
field.usage: Allowing symlinks lets the template engine follow symlinked paths, convenient when developing with linked packages locally. On production it widens the attack surface: anyone able to place a symlink can make Magento render files outside the theme directory, so keep it No. Scoped per website/store.

field.summary: Strips whitespace from rendered HTML to cut page size; has no effect in developer mode.
field.usage: When Yes, page HTML is minified to reduce transfer size. As the native note says, it is skipped in developer mode, so test it in production mode. Changing it affects cached output — flush the page cache to see the result. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Enables in-place editing of storefront translations directly on the page.
field.usage: When Yes, translatable strings on the storefront can be edited inline by an authorised user. A translation/development aid; keep No in production. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Yes turns on in-place translation of Admin text; a dev aid only, and heed the note about disabling caches.
field.usage: When Yes, Admin interface strings can be translated inline in the browser — a development aid, not for production. The native note matters: with block/translate output caches on, your edits won't appear until caches are cleared. Default scope only.

field.summary: Which countries customers may select in address and checkout forms.
field.usage: The set of countries offered in country dropdowns across the store (registration, checkout, addresses). Can differ per website.

field.summary: The country selected by default in address and checkout forms.
field.usage: The pre-selected country in country dropdowns. Can differ per website or store view, so each store can default to its primary market.

field.summary: Countries listed at the top of country dropdowns as quick-pick destinations.
field.usage: Countries pinned to the top of country selectors as frequently used destinations, ahead of the full alphabetical list. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Which countries are treated as part of the European Union.
field.usage: The list of countries the store treats as EU members, used by EU-specific logic such as VAT handling.

field.summary: The countries for which the ZIP/postal code field is not required in addresses.
field.usage: Addresses for the selected countries can be saved without a ZIP/postal code; for all others it stays mandatory.

field.summary: The language/locale used for the store's interface and formatting.
field.usage: The locale that sets the store's language and number/date formatting. Can differ per website or store view, so each store can run in its own language.

field.summary: Which weekday calendars treat as the first day of the week.
field.usage: The day shown first in calendar controls (e.g. Sunday or Monday). Can differ per website or store view to match local convention.

field.summary: The time zone used for storing and displaying store dates and times.
field.usage: The time zone applied to the store's dates and times (orders, reports, schedules). Can differ per website.

field.summary: Which days are treated as the weekend.
field.usage: The days marked as weekend, used by date-based logic. Can differ per website or store view to match local convention.

field.summary: The unit of measure used for product weights.
field.usage: The weight unit applied to products: lbs or kgs. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether the state/province field is shown even for countries where it is optional.
field.usage: When Yes, the state/province selector appears for countries where state is optional, letting customers supply it anyway.

field.summary: The countries for which a state/province must be provided in addresses.
field.usage: Addresses for the selected countries require a state/province to be chosen or entered.

field.summary: Yes hides the store-view switcher and scope selectors to simplify a single-store admin.
field.usage: When Yes, the admin drops store-view switchers and scope selectors for a simpler single-store experience. As the field note says, it is ignored once the system has more than one store view, so it has no effect on a multi-store setup.

field.summary: The store's city, shown in emails and documents.
field.usage: The city of the store's address, displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The store's country, used in emails, documents and address formatting.
field.usage: The country of the store's registered address, shown in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The store's hours of operation shown in emails and documents.
field.usage: Free-text hours of operation displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The store's VAT registration number, shown on applicable documents.
field.usage: The merchant's VAT registration number, displayed in customer-facing templates such as invoices where required. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The store name shown in transactional emails, invoices and similar documents.
field.usage: The store's name as it appears in customer-facing templates such as email headers and printed documents. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The store contact phone number shown in emails and documents.
field.usage: The store phone number displayed in customer-facing templates such as emails and invoices. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The store's ZIP/postal code, shown in emails and documents.
field.usage: The postal code of the store's address, displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The store's region or state, shown in emails and documents.
field.usage: The region/state of the store's address, displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The store's street address, shown in emails and documents.
field.usage: The first line of the store's street address, displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The second line of the store's street address, shown in emails and documents.
field.usage: An optional second line of the store's street address, displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Enables Google AdWords conversion tracking on the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, the AdWords conversion tracking snippet is added to the order success page. Set to No to remove it. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Color of the Google AdWords conversion-tracking snippet; applies only when Google AdWords is enabled.
field.usage: Sets the color value used by the Google AdWords conversion-tracking tag. A backend model validates the entered color. Applies only when Enable Google AdWords is set to Yes. Can differ per website and store view.

field.summary: Format of the conversion value reported to Google AdWords conversion tracking.
field.usage: Sets the conversion-value format sent to Google AdWords conversion tracking. Applies only when AdWords is enabled (google/adwords/active). Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The Google AdWords conversion ID that identifies your account for tracking.
field.usage: The conversion ID issued by Google AdWords, used to attribute storefront conversions to your account. Applies only when Enable is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The Google AdWords conversion label paired with the conversion ID.
field.usage: The conversion label from AdWords that, together with the conversion ID, identifies the specific conversion action being tracked. Applies only when Enable is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The language of the AdWords conversion tracking snippet.
field.usage: Selects the language used by the AdWords conversion tracking code. Applies only when Enable is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The fixed conversion value reported to Google AdWords.
field.usage: The constant value sent with each tracked conversion. Applies only when Enable is Yes and Conversion Value Type is set to a fixed value. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether the tracked conversion value is a fixed amount or taken dynamically from the order.
field.usage: Chooses between reporting a constant conversion value and a value derived from each order. The choice determines whether Conversion Value or Send Order Currency applies. Applies only when Enable is set to Yes.

values.value: Report the actual order value for conversions.
Report a fixed constant value for conversions.

field.summary: Whether to send the order currency with the dynamic conversion value.
field.usage: When Yes, the order's currency is included alongside the conversion value. Applies only when Enable is Yes and Conversion Value Type uses the dynamic order value. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The Google Analytics measurement/tracking ID that storefront data is sent to.
field.usage: The Google Analytics account identifier (tracking/measurement ID) for the storefront. Applies only when Enable is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Enables Google Analytics tracking on the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, the Google Analytics tracking script is added to storefront pages. Can be configured per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether visitor IP addresses are anonymized before being sent to Google Analytics.
field.usage: When Yes, visitor IP addresses are anonymized before being sent to Google Analytics, which helps with privacy compliance. Applies only when Enable is Yes.

field.summary: Enables Google Content Experiments (A/B testing) integration for the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, Google Content Experiments code is injected for A/B testing. Applies only when the associated Google Analytics integration is enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Turns on Google Ads (AdWords) conversion tracking.
field.usage: When Yes, Google Ads conversion tracking is added to the storefront via gtag.js. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Google Ads conversion ID for gtag tracking; applies only when AdWords is active. Can differ per store view.
field.usage: The Google Ads conversion ID (the field note shows the AW-XXXXXXXX form) that the gtag conversion tag reports against. Applies only when Google AdWords tracking is active, and is scoped to website/store so each view can report to its own account.

field.summary: The Google Ads conversion label reported when a conversion occurs.
field.usage: The conversion label from your Google Ads account, used to attribute conversions. Applies only when Google AdWords tracking is enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Turns on Google Analytics 4 tracking via gtag.js.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront loads Google Analytics 4 tracking through gtag.js. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Enables Google Content Experiments (A/B testing) integration for Google Analytics 4.
field.usage: When Yes, Google Content Experiments code is injected for A/B testing under the Google Analytics 4 integration. Applies only when Google Analytics 4 is enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: GA4 Measurement ID tying tracking tags to your Analytics property; must match or no data lands.
field.usage: The GA4 Measurement ID (G-XXXXXXXX) linking storefront tracking tags to your Google Analytics property; it must match that property or no data is recorded. Applies only when the integration is active, and can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Yes disables page cache during Login-as-Customer so personalized pages aren't served to others.
