field.usage: When Yes, Magento collects statistics on product links customers email to friends (per the note), feeding the related report. With it off, no such data is gathered. Applies only when the parent reporting option is enabled. Default scope.

field.summary: Yes logs add-to-cart events for the report, adding some overhead; active only when reporting is enabled.
field.usage: When Yes, add-to-cart events are recorded to populate the 'Product Added To Cart' report, which adds some write overhead. Takes effect only when the parent reporting option is enabled.

field.summary: Collects 'added to wishlist' statistics that power the matching report.
field.usage: When enabled, Magento records products added to wishlists, supplying the data for the 'Product Added To WishList' report. Applies only when the reports feature is enabled. Collecting this adds some database writes. Global scope.

field.summary: Records product-page views to power the Product Views report; adds a write on each view.
field.usage: When Yes, Magento logs product-page views to build the Product Views report. Collecting this data adds a database write per view, so it carries a small performance cost. Applies only when reports collection is enabled. Default scope.

field.summary: Yes collects data for the shared-wishlist report; only useful if you review that report.
field.usage: Yes records statistics for the shared-wishlist report, adding a little logging overhead; it only pays off if you actually review that report. Applies only when the parent reporting option is enabled.

field.summary: The file types customers may attach to an RMA request.
field.usage: The set of file extensions accepted for attachments on a return request; files of other types are rejected. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Max size (MB) per RMA attachment; also bounded by the server's PHP upload limits. Can differ per website.
field.usage: Limits the size, in megabytes, of each file a customer attaches to an RMA. The effective ceiling is still capped by the server's PHP upload_max_filesize/post_max_size, so raising this above those has no effect. Scoped per website.

field.summary: Maximum number of files attachable per RMA submission or comment.
field.usage: Caps how many files a customer can attach in one RMA creation or comment. Lower limits reduce storage use and abuse; higher limits let customers document issues more fully. Website scoped.

field.summary: Template for the admin new-RMA notification email; custom overrides the theme default.
field.usage: Selects which template formats the notification emailed to the admin when a new RMA is created. Default follows theme fallback; a custom template overrides it. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Address that receives admin RMA notification emails; can differ per store view.
field.usage: The email address, per the field note, that receives admin notifications about RMA activity. Scoped to website/store, so returns from different store views can route to different inboxes or teams.

field.summary: Template for the email a customer gets when a new RMA is created; pick a custom one to brand it.
field.usage: Selects the email template sent to the customer when a new RMA is created. Choose a custom template to tailor wording and branding. Set per website/store for store-specific messaging.

field.summary: Email template for the customer notification when an RMA's status changes.
field.usage: The template for the email sent to the customer whenever their RMA (return) changes status. Can differ per website/store view so each storefront can brand the notification.

field.summary: Which store email identity RMA notification emails are sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity used for RMA (return) notification emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2) configured under General → Store Email Addresses. Can be set per store view.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Turns RMA return handling on or off; can differ per website.
field.usage: Enables or disables the RMA return-management functionality, as the field note says. Turning it Yes exposes the return request flows to customers and staff. Scoped to website, so RMA can run on some websites but not others.

field.summary: Text prepended to generated RMA numbers (e.g. RMA-); identification only, no functional effect. Can differ per website.
field.usage: A string placed in front of each generated RMA increment ID to make returns easy to recognise. It is purely for identification and does not affect RMA processing. Scoped per website, so separate sites can use distinct prefixes.

field.summary: Days after order completion a customer may still request a return.
field.usage: The window, in days from order completion, during which returns can be requested; after it, customers can no longer open an RMA. Website scoped, so return policy can vary per store.

field.summary: Order statuses that are eligible for return requests; orders in other statuses won't offer an RMA option.
field.usage: Selects which order statuses allow a customer to open a return (RMA) request (native note). Orders whose status isn't chosen here won't show a return option. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Yes auto-approves new return requests, skipping manual review — faster for customers, but no gate against bad returns.
field.usage: When Yes, new RMA (return) requests are approved automatically instead of waiting for staff review (per the note). This speeds the customer's return but removes the manual check against invalid or fraudulent requests. Set per website.

field.summary: Enables a per-category product RSS feed.
field.usage: When enabled, shoppers can subscribe to an RSS feed of products within a top-level category.

field.summary: Enables the RSS feed of coupons and discounts.
field.usage: When enabled, a public RSS feed of current coupons and discounts is published. (RSS feeds must also be enabled globally.) Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Enables the RSS feed of new products.
field.usage: When enabled, a public RSS feed of newly added products is published. (RSS feeds must also be enabled globally.)

field.summary: Enables the RSS feed of special-price (sale) products.
field.usage: When enabled, a public RSS feed of products on special price is published.

field.summary: Enables RSS feed generation across the storefront.
field.usage: Enables or disables RSS feeds site-wide. Individual feeds (catalog, wishlist, and others) require this master switch to be enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether the customer order status RSS feed is available.
field.usage: When Enabled, customers can subscribe to an RSS feed that reports their order status changes. Options are Enable and Disable. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Enables an RSS feed for shared wish lists.
field.usage: When enabled, a shared wish list can be followed via RSS. Options are Enable and Disable. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Whether rate limiting is applied to order placement requests.
field.usage: When Yes, the number of order-placement requests is capped per customer and per guest to protect the store from bursts of checkout traffic. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Maximum order-placement requests allowed per guest in the period.
field.usage: The cap on how many order-placement requests a single guest may make within the configured reset period. Applies only when rate limiting is enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Maximum order-placement requests allowed per authenticated customer in the period.
field.usage: The cap on how many order-placement requests a single signed-in customer may make within the configured reset period. Applies only when rate limiting is enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The length of the time window after which the request counter resets.
field.usage: Selects the time period over which order-placement requests are counted before the per-customer and per-guest limits reset. Applies only when rate limiting is enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

values.value: Measure the request limit per minute.
Measure the request limit per hour.
Measure the request limit per day.

field.summary: Whether customers can cancel their own orders through GraphQL.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can cancel eligible orders through the GraphQL API. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The list of reasons a customer can choose from when cancelling an order.
field.usage: Defines the selectable reasons offered to customers when they cancel an order. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Yes reads the dashboard from aggregated tables (fast, not realtime); No uses live data (slower).
field.usage: Yes draws the admin dashboard from pre-aggregated report tables, which is fast but only as current as the last report aggregation (cron). No queries live sales data: accurate but slower on busy stores.

values.value: Send one email and blind-copy the extra recipients.
Send each recipient a separate copy of the email.

field.summary: Extra recipients copied on credit-memo comment emails; applies only when those emails are enabled.

field.summary: Whether an email is sent when a comment is added to a credit memo.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.

field.summary: Whether the credit memo email is sent.

Choosing Default falls back to the theme's template (native note). Applies only when credit memo emails are enabled (depends). Can differ per website/store view.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.

field.summary: Email template for the credit-memo (refund) notice; applies only when credit memo emails are enabled.
field.usage: The template for the credit memo email that notifies a customer of a refund. Leave Default for theme fallback (per the note), or choose a custom template to brand it. Applies only when credit memo emails are enabled. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether sales emails are queued and sent in the background rather than immediately.
field.usage: When Enabled, sales emails are sent asynchronously through the message queue and cron instead of at the moment of the action. Options are Enable and Disable.

field.summary: Caps how many sales emails are processed per cron run; applies only when async sending is on.
field.usage: Limits how many entities (orders, shipments, etc.) are processed in a single cron run, as the field note says. Applies only when asynchronous email sending is enabled; lower it to ease load per run, raise it to clear the queue faster.

field.summary: How copies of the invoice comment email are sent — as Bcc or as a separate email.

values.value: Send one email and blind-copy the extra recipients.

field.summary: Which store email identity the invoice comment email is sent from.

field.usage: Chooses whether copies of the invoice email are sent as a Bcc on the customer's email or as a Separate Email. Applies only when the invoice email is enabled. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Which store email identity the invoice email is sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender for invoice emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2). Applies only when the invoice email is enabled. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Which store email identity the order comment email is sent from.

field.usage: Selects the sender for order confirmation emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2). Applies only when the order email is enabled. Can differ per store view.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.

field.summary: Template for the new-order confirmation email; applies only when order emails are enabled. 'Default' resolves via theme fallback. Per website/store.
field.usage: The email template used for the order confirmation sent when an order is placed. Applies only when order emails are enabled; 'Default' resolves through theme fallback. Can be set per website/store view.

field.summary: How copies of the shipment comment email are sent — as Bcc or as a separate email.
field.usage: Chooses whether copies of the shipment comment email are sent as a Bcc on the customer's email or as a Separate Email. Applies only when the shipment comment email is enabled. Can differ per store view.

values.value: Send one email and blind-copy the extra recipients.
Send each recipient a separate copy of the email.

field.summary: Extra addresses copied on shipment-comment emails; comma-separated.
field.usage: Additional recipients who receive a copy of shipment-comment emails, entered comma-separated. Useful for a warehouse or support mailbox. Applies only when shipment emails are enabled. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Whether an email is sent when a comment is added to a shipment.
field.usage: When Yes, the customer is emailed when a comment is added to a shipment. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Template for shipment-comment emails to guest (non-registered) buyers; applies only when shipment emails are enabled. Per website/store.
field.usage: The email template for shipment-comment notifications sent to guest customers specifically; registered customers use their own template. Applies only when shipment emails are enabled; 'Default' resolves via theme fallback. Per website/store.

field.summary: Which store email identity the shipment comment email is sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender for shipment comment emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2). Applies only when the shipment comment email is enabled. Can differ per store view.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Email template for shipment-comment notifications; applies only when shipment emails are enabled. Can differ per store view.
field.usage: The template used when a comment is added to a shipment and emailed to the customer. As the field note says, Default resolves through theme fallback. Applies only when shipment comment emails are enabled, and is scoped per store view.

field.summary: How copies of the shipment email are sent — as Bcc or as a separate email.
field.usage: Chooses whether copies of the shipment email are sent as a Bcc on the customer's email or as a Separate Email. Applies only when the shipment email is enabled. Can differ per store view.

values.value: Send one email and blind-copy the extra recipients.
Send each recipient a separate copy of the email.

field.summary: Comma-separated addresses that get a copy of every shipment email; needs shipment emails on.
field.usage: A comma-separated list of addresses that each receive a copy of every shipment email, useful for warehouse or monitoring inboxes. Applies only when shipment emails are enabled, and can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether the shipment email is sent.
field.usage: When Yes, an email is sent to the customer when a shipment is created for their order. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Email template for shipment emails sent to guest (non-registered) customers.
field.usage: The template for shipment notification emails sent to guest customers. Applies only when shipment emails are enabled; Default follows theme fallback. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Which store email identity the shipment email is sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender for shipment emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2). Applies only when the shipment email is enabled. Can differ per store view.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Template for shipment notification emails; only sent when shipment emails are enabled.
field.usage: Selects the template for shipment notification emails sent to customers. Applies only when shipment emails are enabled; a custom template overrides the theme default. Set per website/store for branding.

field.summary: Yes hides the customer IP on orders, invoices, shipments and credit memos (privacy/GDPR).
field.usage: Yes stops the stored customer IP address from appearing on orders, invoices, shipments and credit memos, which helps with privacy and GDPR obligations. It affects what is shown, not whether the IP was recorded. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether shoppers can add a gift message to individual order items.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can attach a separate gift message to each item in the order during checkout. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether shoppers can add a single gift message to the whole order.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can attach one gift message at the order level during checkout. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The store address printed on invoices and packing slips.
field.usage: The address block shown in the header of printed invoices and packing slips. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Logo image used on PDF invoices and packing slips; can differ per store view.
field.usage: The logo placed on printed PDF invoices and packing slips. As the field note says, it accepts jpeg/tiff/png and a larger file helps if the PDF image looks distorted. Scoped to website/store, so each store view can print its own branding.

field.summary: Logo shown on HTML (on-screen) invoice and packing-slip views, not the PDF versions; blank uses the default. Per website/store.
field.usage: The logo used on the HTML print view of invoices and packing slips, not the PDF documents, which take a separate logo. Accepts jpeg/gif/png; leave it empty to fall back to the default. Settable per website/store so each brand can show its own.

field.summary: Yes shows the one-click Instant Purchase button using a customer's stored card and address; needs a vault-capable payment method.
field.usage: When Yes, logged-in customers get a one-click Instant Purchase button that checks out with their saved (vaulted) payment token and default addresses. As the native note says, a payment method supporting vault and instant purchase must be enabled first. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: The label shown on the Instant Purchase button.
field.usage: The text displayed on the Instant Purchase button that lets customers check out in one click. Applies only when Instant Purchase is enabled. Can be set per store view for localised wording.

field.summary: Whether a minimum order amount is required before checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, orders whose total is below the configured minimum amount cannot be placed. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Smallest order subtotal (after discount) allowed through checkout.
field.usage: The minimum order value required to place an order, measured on the subtotal after discounts per the native note. Carts below it are blocked at checkout. Website scoped, so the threshold can differ per store.

field.summary: Message shown in the cart when the discounted subtotal is below the minimum order amount; can be localized per store view.
field.usage: The text displayed in the shopping cart when the subtotal after discount falls below the minimum allowed order amount (native note). Because it's store-view scoped, you can tailor or translate it per store view. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: The message shown in the cart when the order is below the minimum amount.
field.usage: The error text displayed in the shopping cart when the order total is below the minimum order amount. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Yes measures the minimum order amount after discounts; discounted carts can then fall below the threshold.
field.usage: Decides whether the minimum order amount is checked against the subtotal after discount (Yes) or the plain subtotal (No), per the note. With Yes, a discount can pull a cart under the minimum and block checkout. Set per website.

field.summary: Whether each address must meet the minimum order amount in multi-address checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, the minimum order amount is validated for each shipping address separately during multi-address checkout, rather than against the order as a whole. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Overrides the default minimum-order message on multi-address checkout; leave empty to use the default.
field.usage: Custom message shown for the minimum order amount during multi-address checkout. Leave it empty to fall back to the default description configured above. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Custom message shown when a multi-address order is below the minimum order amount.
field.usage: The error shown in the cart when an order shipped to multiple addresses falls below the minimum order amount. Leave it empty to reuse the default minimum-order error. Can differ per website/store view.

technical.default_value: The current cart does not match multi shipping criteria, please review or contact the store administrator

field.summary: Whether the minimum order amount is compared with tax included.
field.usage: Chooses whether the order total is checked against the minimum amount including tax or excluding it. Can differ per website.

field.summary: When the actual price is revealed for products using a Minimum Advertised Price.
field.usage: Chooses where the real price is shown instead of the MAP: On Gesture (after a click/popup), In Cart, or Before Order Confirmation. Can differ per website.

values.value: Reveal the price when the shopper acts (hover/click gesture).
Reveal the price only once the product is in the cart.
Reveal the price just before order confirmation.

field.summary: Yes turns on Minimum Advertised Price store-wide — and, per the warning, hides all storefront prices until a MAP action.
field.usage: Enables Minimum Advertised Price (MAP) handling as the store default. The native warning is key: turning it Yes hides product prices on the storefront until the configured action (such as adding to cart) reveals them. Set per website.

field.summary: The default text shown in the MAP price popup.
field.usage: The message displayed in the popup that explains why the actual price is hidden for Minimum Advertised Price products. Can differ per website or store view.

technical.default_value:
Our price is lower than the manufacturer's "minimum advertised price." As a result, we cannot show you the price in catalog or the product page.

You have no obligation to purchase the product once you know the price. You can simply remove the item from your cart.

field.summary: The default text shown in the MAP "What's This" popup.
field.usage: The message displayed in the "What's This" popup linked from Minimum Advertised Price products. Can differ per website or store view.

technical.default_value:
Our price is lower than the manufacturer's "minimum advertised price." As a result, we cannot show you the price in catalog or the product page.

You have no obligation to purchase the product once you know the price. You can simply remove the item from your cart.

field.summary: How long, in minutes, a pending-payment order is kept before it is cancelled.
field.usage: The lifetime in minutes for orders awaiting payment; a scheduled job cancels orders older than this. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether the order ID is shown in the header of printed credit memos.
field.usage: When Yes, the order ID is printed in the header of the credit memo PDF. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Whether the order ID is shown in the header of printed invoices.
field.usage: When Yes, the order ID is printed in the header of the invoice PDF. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Whether the order ID is shown in the header of printed shipments.
field.usage: When Yes, the order ID is printed in the header of the shipment (packing slip) PDF. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Whether customers can reorder a previous order from their account.
field.usage: When Yes, the Reorder action is available in the customer account and order history, letting shoppers place a new order based on a past one. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: The position of the Discount line among the cart and checkout totals, as a sort order number.
field.usage: A numeric sort order that sets where the Discount line appears in the totals block of the cart and checkout. Lower numbers appear higher. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The position of the Grand Total line among the cart and checkout totals, as a sort order number.
field.usage: A numeric sort order that sets where the Grand Total line appears in the totals block of the cart and checkout. Lower numbers appear higher. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The position of the Shipping line among the cart and checkout totals, as a sort order number.
field.usage: A numeric sort order that sets where the Shipping line appears in the totals block of the cart and checkout. Lower numbers appear higher. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The position of the Subtotal line among the cart and checkout totals, as a sort order number.
field.usage: A numeric sort order that sets where the Subtotal line appears in the totals block of the cart and checkout. Lower numbers appear higher. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The position of the Tax line among the cart and checkout totals, as a sort order number.
field.usage: A numeric sort order that sets where the Tax line appears in the totals block of the cart and checkout. Lower numbers appear higher. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The position of the Fixed Product Tax line among the order totals.
field.usage: A sort-order number that sets where the Fixed Product Tax line appears relative to the other totals (subtotal, shipping, tax, etc.). Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether a credit memo with a zero grand total can be created.
field.usage: When Yes, a credit memo can be issued even when its grand total comes to zero. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Whether guests, not only signed-in customers, can use Email to a Friend.
field.usage: When Yes, visitors who are not signed in can send the Email to a Friend product share. Applies only when the feature is enabled. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: How senders are identified when enforcing the Email to a Friend sending limits.
field.usage: Selects the method used to identify a sender when applying the sending limits. Applies only when the feature is enabled. Can be set per website or store view.

values.value: Count send-to-friend limits by IP address.
Count send-to-friend limits by cookie (can be cleared — less safe).

field.summary: Yes enables Email to a Friend; pair with CAPTCHA since it sends mail on a visitor's behalf.
field.usage: Yes exposes the Email to a Friend product-sharing feature on the storefront. Because it sends mail on a visitor's behalf it is a spam vector, so enable a CAPTCHA alongside it. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The maximum number of products a sender can share by email within one hour.
field.usage: Rate limit for how many products a single sender may share via Email to a Friend within one hour. Applies only when the feature is enabled. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The maximum number of recipients allowed per Email to a Friend message.
field.usage: The maximum number of recipient addresses allowed in a single Email to a Friend message. Applies only when the feature is enabled. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Template for the Email-to-a-Friend message; applies only when the feature is enabled. Can differ per store view.
field.usage: The email template used by the Email to a Friend feature. As the field note says, Default resolves through theme fallback. Applies only when the feature is enabled, and is scoped per store view.

field.summary: The city the store ships from.
field.usage: The city of the store's shipping origin address. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The country the store ships from, used as the origin for shipping-rate calculation.
field.usage: The country of the store's shipping origin. Carriers use it as the starting point when calculating shipping rates and estimating delivery. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The ZIP or postal code the store ships from.
field.usage: The postal code of the store's shipping origin, used by carriers to calculate shipping rates. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The state or region the store ships from.
field.usage: The region or state of the store's shipping origin, paired with the origin country for rate calculation. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The street address the store ships from.
field.usage: The street address of the store's shipping origin. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The second line of the store's shipping origin street address.
field.usage: An optional second line for the shipping origin street address. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether a custom shipping policy is shown to customers at checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, the custom shipping policy text is displayed to customers during checkout. Set to No to hide it. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The custom shipping policy text shown to customers.
field.usage: The shipping policy wording displayed at checkout. Applies only when Apply custom Shipping Policy is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The changefreq hint written for category URLs in the XML sitemap.
field.usage: How often category pages are declared to change, as the sitemap <changefreq> value: always, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly or never. A hint to crawlers, not a guarantee.

values.value: Hint to crawlers that the page changes every visit.
Hint that the page changes about hourly.
Hint that the page changes about daily.
Hint that the page changes about weekly.
Hint that the page changes about monthly.
Hint that the page changes about yearly.
Hint that the page is archived and won't change.

field.summary: The <priority> value (0.0-1.0) for category URLs in the XML sitemap; a relative hint to crawlers, not a guarantee. Per website/store.
field.usage: Sets the <priority> hint (0.0 to 1.0) written for category URLs in the generated XML sitemap, signalling their importance relative to other URLs. Search engines treat it only as a hint, so it influences crawl weighting rather than rankings. Per website/store.

field.summary: Turns scheduled automatic sitemap generation on or off.
field.usage: When Yes, the sitemap is regenerated automatically on a schedule (see the Frequency and Start Time below). When No, it is only generated manually.

field.summary: Email address that receives a notice if scheduled sitemap generation fails.
field.usage: Where the failure notification is sent when a scheduled sitemap run errors. Applies only when scheduled generation is Enabled.

field.summary: Which store email identity the sitemap error notice is sent from.
field.usage: The sender identity for the generation-failure email, chosen from the Store Email Addresses identities. Applies only when scheduled generation is Enabled.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Email template for notifications when scheduled sitemap generation fails.
field.usage: The template for the email sent when scheduled XML sitemap generation fails. Applies only when error notifications are enabled; Default follows theme fallback. Can differ per website.

field.summary: How often the scheduled sitemap regeneration runs.
field.usage: The cadence of the automatic sitemap run. Applies only when scheduled generation is Enabled.

values.value: Run once a day.
Run once a week.
Run once a month.

field.summary: Choose Batch for large catalogs to avoid running out of memory during sitemap generation.
field.usage: Selects how the XML sitemap is built: the standard method holds all data in memory, while the batch method uses memory-optimised processing. Choose batch for large catalogs to avoid memory exhaustion. Applies only when the sitemap is enabled. Can differ per website/store.

values.value: Build the whole sitemap in memory in one pass.
Build the sitemap in smaller batches to use less memory on large catalogs.

field.summary: Time of day the scheduled sitemap generation runs.
field.usage: The hour and minute at which the automatic sitemap run is scheduled. Applies only when scheduled generation is Enabled.

field.summary: Max bytes per sitemap file; larger sitemaps split into several files under an index.
field.usage: When a generated XML sitemap would exceed this size (in bytes), it is split into multiple files tied together by a sitemap index, keeping each file within search-engine limits. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Maximum number of URLs written to a single sitemap file before it is split.
field.usage: Caps how many URLs go into one sitemap file; once exceeded, Magento writes additional files and a sitemap index. Keep within the sitemaps.org limit of 50,000 URLs per file.

field.summary: The changefreq hint written for CMS page URLs in the XML sitemap.
field.usage: How often CMS pages are declared to change in the sitemap (<changefreq>): always, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly or never.

values.value: Hint to crawlers that the page changes every visit.
Hint that the page changes about hourly.
Hint that the page changes about daily.
Hint that the page changes about weekly.
Hint that the page changes about monthly.
Hint that the page changes about yearly.
Hint that the page is archived and won't change.

field.summary: Priority (0.0-1.0) written for CMS pages in the XML sitemap; a crawl hint search engines may ignore.
field.usage: The priority value, from 0.0 to 1.0 (per the note), written for CMS pages in the XML sitemap to signal their relative importance to crawlers. It is only a hint — search engines may disregard it — and is relative within your own site. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: The changefreq hint written for product URLs in the XML sitemap.
field.usage: How often product pages are declared to change in the sitemap (<changefreq>): always, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly or never.

values.value: Hint to crawlers that the page changes every visit.
Hint that the page changes about hourly.
Hint that the page changes about daily.
Hint that the page changes about weekly.
Hint that the page changes about monthly.
Hint that the page changes about yearly.
Hint that the page is archived and won't change.

field.summary: Whether product images are added to sitemap entries, and which ones.
field.usage: Controls product image inclusion in the sitemap: None, the Base Only image, or All gallery images.

field.summary: Crawl-priority hint (0.0–1.0) given to product URLs in the XML sitemap.
field.usage: Sets the <priority> value for product URLs in the generated sitemap, from 0.0 to 1.0, hinting their relative importance to crawlers. It is only a hint — search engines may ignore it. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Whether the sitemap's location is added to robots.txt.
field.usage: When Yes, a Sitemap: line pointing at the generated file is written into robots.txt so crawlers can discover it.

field.summary: The changefreq hint written for the store/home URL in the XML sitemap.
field.usage: How often the store home URL is declared to change in the sitemap (<changefreq>): always, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly or never.

values.value: Hint to crawlers that the page changes every visit.
Hint that the page changes about hourly.
Hint that the page changes about daily.
Hint that the page changes about weekly.
Hint that the page changes about monthly.
Hint that the page changes about yearly.
Hint that the page is archived and won't change.

field.summary: Priority hint (0.0–1.0) written into the XML sitemap for store URLs, signalling relative importance to crawlers.
field.usage: Sets the <priority> value for store URLs in the generated XML sitemap, hinting their importance relative to other pages (valid 0.0–1.0, native note). Higher suggests greater importance, but crawlers may ignore the hint. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: How often the admin checks the notification feed for new messages.
field.usage: The interval at which Magento polls its notifications feed for new messages. Choose a longer interval to check less frequently.

field.summary: Whether the admin fetches the notification feed over HTTPS.
field.usage: When Yes, the Magento notifications feed is retrieved over a secure HTTPS connection rather than plain HTTP.

field.summary: Yes closes open menus when a page is restored from back/forward cache, so a menu left open doesn't reappear open.
field.usage: When Yes, menus left open are closed when the browser restores the page from its back/forward cache, preventing a stale open menu from reappearing on navigation. Works only with compatible themes (native note). Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Lets browsers keep whole pages in memory for instant back/forward; may show stale content.
field.usage: When Yes, enables the browser back/forward cache so revisited pages load instantly from memory. The tradeoff is that dynamic content such as the cart or prices can appear stale on back navigation. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Yes defers the mini-cart refresh until the shopper interacts after a bfcache restore, protecting page-speed scores.
field.usage: On a bfcache page restore, Yes refreshes the mini cart only after the shopper interacts, while No refreshes immediately (per the note). Deferring avoids a JS/layout cost on restore, helping Core Web Vitals; the trade-off is a briefly stale cart count. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Pages matching these substrings skip the back/forward cache; exclude cart, checkout and account pages.
field.usage: URL substrings (one per line) that exclude matching pages from the browser back/forward cache. Use it for dynamic or personalised pages — cart, checkout, account — that must not be restored from a cached snapshot. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: How many days bulk (asynchronous) operation log entries are kept before being purged.
field.usage: The retention period, in days, for bulk action log records; older entries are removed after this many days.

field.summary: How often (in minutes) completed cron history for the consumers group is purged.
field.usage: Interval, in minutes, between cleanups of the cron schedule history for the message-queue consumers group. Older success/failure records are removed on this cadence. Global scope.

field.summary: How long records of failed cron jobs in the consumers group are kept before cleanup removes them.
field.usage: Retention period for failed cron schedule records belonging to the consumers group; once older than this they are purged during cron history cleanup. A global (default-scope) setting.

field.summary: How long (minutes) successful cron job records are kept before cleanup.
field.usage: Retention period, in minutes, for successfully completed jobs of the consumers cron group in the schedule table; older success records are purged during history cleanup.

field.summary: How far ahead cron schedules jobs for the consumers group, in minutes.
field.usage: The time, in minutes, that cron pre-schedules jobs for the consumers group. A larger value queues jobs further in advance. Global (default scope).

field.summary: How often (in minutes) cron schedules are generated for the consumers group.
field.usage: The interval, in minutes, at which Magento pre-generates schedule rows for the consumers cron group. A larger value means fewer, larger batches of scheduled jobs. Global setting.

field.summary: Minutes after its scheduled time a 'consumers' cron job may still run before it's marked missed.
field.usage: The grace window, in minutes, for the consumers cron group: a job not started within this many minutes of its scheduled time is flagged as missed instead of run.

field.summary: Whether the consumers cron group runs in its own PHP process.
field.usage: When Yes, jobs in the message-queue consumers cron group run in a separate process from other cron groups, isolating their execution. Global scope.

field.summary: How often cron history cleanup runs for the default job group.
field.usage: The interval at which Magento purges old cron schedule records for the default group. A global (default-scope) setting.

field.summary: How long (minutes) failed or errored cron job records are kept before cleanup.
field.usage: Retention period, in minutes, for failed or errored jobs of the default cron group in the schedule table; older failure records are purged during history cleanup.

field.summary: How long successful cron job records are kept for the default group, in minutes.
field.usage: The retention period, in minutes, for successfully completed cron job records in the default group before they are cleaned from the schedule table. Global (default scope).

field.summary: How far ahead (in minutes) schedules are generated for the default cron group.
field.usage: How far into the future, in minutes, Magento pre-creates schedule rows for the default cron group. It sets the window of pending jobs that the generator fills. Global setting.

field.summary: How often (in minutes) cron schedule entries are generated for the 'default' group.
field.usage: Sets how frequently Magento pre-generates upcoming schedule rows for the default cron group, in minutes.

field.summary: Grace period (in minutes) before a pending default-group job is marked missed.
field.usage: If a scheduled job in the default cron group is not executed within this many minutes of its scheduled time, it is flagged as 'missed' rather than run. Global scope.

field.summary: Yes runs the default group's cron jobs in their own PHP process instead of the main cron run.
field.usage: Yes/No. When Yes, cron jobs in the default group are executed in a separate PHP process, isolating them from other groups in the same cron run. A global (default-scope) setting.

field.summary: How often (minutes) old cron history records are purged.
field.usage: Interval, in minutes, between cleanups of the index cron group's old schedule history — how frequently expired success and failure records are removed.

field.summary: How long failed cron job records are kept for the index group, in minutes.
field.usage: The retention period, in minutes, for failed cron job records in the index group before they are cleaned from the schedule table. Global (default scope).

field.summary: How long (in minutes) successful job records are kept for the index cron group.
field.usage: The retention period, in minutes, for successfully completed job history in the index cron group; older success records are pruned by cleanup. Global setting.

field.summary: How far ahead (in minutes) schedules are generated for the 'index' cron group.
field.usage: How many minutes into the future Magento pre-creates schedule rows for the index cron group, so jobs are queued before their run time.

field.summary: How often (in minutes) the indexer cron group pre-generates its schedule entries.
field.usage: Interval, in minutes, at which Magento generates upcoming schedule rows for the index cron group. Global scope.

field.summary: Grace window after a scheduled time within which an index-group job must run, or it is marked missed.
field.usage: How long after its scheduled time a cron job in the index group may still start; if it has not run within this window the schedule is flagged as missed. A global (default-scope) setting.

field.summary: Yes runs this cron group in its own PHP process, separate from other groups.
field.usage: When Yes, the index cron group runs in a separate PHP process from the main cron, isolating its jobs so they don't block other groups. When No, it shares the main process.

field.summary: How often, in minutes, completed cron history for this group is cleaned up.
field.usage: The interval, in minutes, between clean-ups of old schedule history records for this cron group.

field.summary: How long, in minutes, failed job records are kept before cleanup.
field.usage: How many minutes records of failed jobs are retained in the schedule table before being removed, for this cron group.

field.summary: How long, in minutes, successful job records are kept before cleanup.
field.usage: How many minutes records of successfully completed jobs are retained in the schedule table before being removed, for this cron group.

field.summary: How far ahead, in minutes, cron jobs are pre-generated for this group.
field.usage: How many minutes into the future schedule rows are created, so jobs for this cron group are queued before their run time.

field.summary: How often, in minutes, upcoming cron schedule rows are pre-generated for this group.
field.usage: The interval, in minutes, at which pending jobs for this cron group are written ahead into the schedule table.

field.summary: The window, in minutes, after which an un-run scheduled job is marked missed.
field.usage: If a scheduled job for this group has not started within this many minutes of its due time, it is marked as missed rather than run.

field.summary: Whether this cron group's jobs run in a separate PHP process.
field.usage: When Yes, jobs in this cron group are executed in their own PHP process, isolating them from other groups.

field.summary: How often cron history is cleaned up for the translate_products group, in minutes.
field.usage: The interval, in minutes, between cleanups of cron job history for the translate_products group. Global (default scope).

field.summary: How long (in minutes) failed job records are kept for the translate_products cron group.
field.usage: The retention period, in minutes, for failed job history in the translate_products cron group; older failure records are pruned by cleanup. Global setting.

field.summary: How long (in minutes) successful 'translate_products' cron records are kept.
field.usage: Retention time, in minutes, for successfully completed job records in the translate_products cron group before they are cleaned up.

field.summary: How far ahead (in minutes) schedules are pre-generated for the translate_products group.
field.usage: The window, in minutes, for which Magento pre-generates upcoming schedule entries for the translate_products cron group. Global scope.

field.summary: How often Magento pre-generates upcoming schedule entries for the translate_products cron group.
field.usage: The interval at which future cron schedule rows are generated for the translate_products group. A global (default-scope) setting.

field.summary: Grace window (minutes) after the scheduled time before a job is marked missed.
field.usage: How many minutes after its scheduled time a translate_products cron job may still start; if it hasn't run within this window it is marked missed rather than executed.

field.summary: Whether the translate_products cron group runs in its own process.
field.usage: When Yes, jobs in the translate_products cron group run in a separate process, isolating them from other groups; No runs them in the shared process. Global (default scope).

field.summary: How often (in minutes) job history is cleaned up for the translate_select_attributes cron group.
field.usage: The interval, in minutes, between cleanup runs that purge aged job-history rows for the translate_select_attributes cron group (using the success/failure lifetimes). Global setting.

field.summary: How long (in minutes) failed 'translate_select_attributes' cron records are kept.
field.usage: Retention time, in minutes, for failed job records in the translate_select_attributes cron group before they are cleaned up.

field.summary: How long (in minutes) successful job records are kept in the group's cron history.
field.usage: Retention, in minutes, for successfully completed job records in the translate_select_attributes cron group before they are cleaned up. Global scope.

field.summary: How far into the future schedule entries are generated for the translate_select_attributes cron group.
field.usage: How far ahead cron schedule rows are pre-created for the translate_select_attributes group. A global (default-scope) setting.

field.summary: How often (minutes) future cron schedule entries are generated ahead of time.
field.usage: Interval, in minutes, at which the translate_select_attributes cron group pre-generates future schedule entries in the cron_schedule table.

field.summary: Window, in minutes, after which a missed translate_select_attributes job is marked missed.
field.usage: If a scheduled job in the translate_select_attributes group does not start within this many minutes of its planned time, it is marked as missed rather than run late. Global (default scope).

field.summary: Whether the translate_select_attributes cron group runs in its own PHP process.
field.usage: When Yes, jobs in the translate_select_attributes cron group run in a separate PHP process, isolating them from other groups so a long or stuck job does not block them. Global setting.

field.summary: The full set of currencies available for use as allowed or display currencies.
field.usage: The currencies installed for the store, forming the pool from which Allowed Currencies and the Default Display Currency are chosen.

field.summary: Selects which application handles full page caching.
field.usage: Chooses the full page caching backend — the built-in Magento cache or an external caching application such as Varnish. The Varnish Configuration options apply when Varnish is selected.

values.value: Use Magento's built-in PHP full-page cache.
Use Varnish as the full-page cache (recommended for production).

field.summary: Caps how many layout handles feed the full-page-cache key; too small risks wrong cached content, too large hurts performance (50–100 suggested).
field.usage: Limits how many layout handles are hashed into the full-page cache key. Too small a value can make different pages share one cache entry (wrong content shown); too large slows cache lookups — the native note suggests 50–100. Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Seconds public pages stay cached before regenerating (empty = 86400); longer lifts hit rate but serves stale content longer.
field.usage: How long, in seconds, public (non-personalised) content stays in the full page cache before it's regenerated; an empty field saves the 86400 default (per the note). A longer TTL raises the cache hit rate but serves stale pages longer after content changes. Default scope.

field.summary: IPs allowed to purge Varnish; only relevant when Varnish is the cache, defaults to localhost if empty.
field.usage: Comma-separated IPs written into the generated Varnish VCL that are permitted to issue purge requests. Relevant only when the caching application is Varnish. If left empty, localhost is saved as the default.

field.summary: Magento backend host written into the generated Varnish config; defaults to localhost if empty.
field.usage: The backend (Magento) host written into the generated Varnish VCL. Applies only when the caching application is Varnish. If left empty, localhost is saved. Set it to the host Varnish should forward cache misses to.

field.summary: Backend port in the generated Varnish config; must match your web server port (empty saves 8080).
field.usage: The port written into the generated Varnish config pointing back at Magento; it must match the port your web server listens on or Varnish cannot reach the backend. Empty saves the default 8080. Applies only when Varnish is the caching application.

field.summary: Caches 404 responses in Varnish; applies only when Varnish is the caching application.
field.usage: Beyond caching Not-Found pages: this takes effect only when Full Page Cache is set to use Varnish. Caching 404s spares the backend from repeated hits on missing URLs, but cached 404s persist until purged.

field.summary: Allows the browser back/forward cache (bfcache) when serving pages through Varnish.
field.usage: Enables back/forward cache support so browsers can instantly restore pages on back/forward navigation. Applies only when the caching application is Varnish. See web.dev for details. Global scope.

field.summary: Yes lets Varnish cache media files as well as pages; applies only when Varnish is the caching application.
field.usage: Yes/No. When Yes, media files are included in Varnish caching rather than only HTML pages. Applies only when the caching application is set to Varnish. A global (default-scope) setting.

field.summary: Yes lets Varnish cache static files as well as pages.
field.usage: When Yes, Varnish also caches static files, not just full pages. Applies only when the Caching Application is set to Varnish. Set at the default scope.

field.summary: Downloads a Varnish 6 configuration (VCL) file based on the current cache settings.
field.usage: Generates and downloads a Varnish 6 VCL configuration file from the current cache settings. Shown in the Varnish Configuration group when Varnish is selected as the caching application.

field.summary: Downloads a Varnish 7 configuration (VCL) file based on the current cache settings.
field.usage: Generates and downloads a Varnish 7 VCL configuration file from the current cache settings. Shown in the Varnish Configuration group when Varnish is selected as the caching application.

field.summary: Varnish grace window, in seconds, for serving stale cached content; applies only when Varnish is the cache.
field.usage: The grace period written into the generated Varnish config. As the field note says, an empty value saves 300 seconds; within it stale content is served while a fresh copy is fetched, and if the backend is unhealthy cached content is served for up to 3 days. Applies only when Varnish is the caching application.

field.summary: Regexes that force matching requests to bypass Varnish and hit the backend.
field.usage: A list of regular expressions matched against request cookie values; a match makes Varnish bypass its cache and pass the request straight to the Magento backend. Applies only when Varnish is the selected caching application. Global (default scope).

field.summary: Query parameters stripped from incoming requests to raise the Varnish cache hit rate.
field.usage: Beyond the native note: these tracking query parameters are removed from incoming URLs before caching, so requests that differ only by them (e.g. campaign tags) still match one cached page. Stored as a serialized list and applied only when Varnish is the selected caching application (its dependency). Global setting.

field.summary: Marks cached pages stale instead of deleting them on purge; needs the Xkey vmod.
field.usage: Soft purging flags cached objects as stale rather than removing them, so Varnish can keep serving the old page while it fetches a fresh copy — smoother than hard purges under load. Requires the Xkey vmod.

field.summary: Uses the Varnish xkey vmod for tag-based cache invalidation instead of the default purge.
field.usage: When Yes, Magento uses the Varnish xkey vmod for more efficient, tag-based cache invalidation. Requires the xkey vmod to be installed in your Varnish instance. Global scope.

field.summary: Whether the legacy (old) media gallery is used instead of the enhanced one.
field.usage: When Yes, the old media gallery interface is used for managing images and media; when No, the enhanced media gallery is used.

field.summary: Turns on generation of optimized, resized renditions of media gallery images.
field.usage: When Yes, Magento generates optimized renditions (smaller resized copies) of media gallery images. Set to No to turn rendition generation off.

field.summary: Max height (px) for optimized media-gallery renditions; lower saves storage and bandwidth but reduces detail. Applies to new renditions.
field.usage: Caps the height, in pixels, of the optimized renditions generated for media-gallery images. Lowering it saves storage and speeds delivery at the cost of detail. It shapes renditions created after the change, not ones already generated.

field.summary: Maximum width, in pixels, for optimized media-gallery renditions.
field.usage: The maximum width in pixels, as the field note says, for the optimized rendition copies generated for media-gallery images. Images wider than this are scaled down to produce lighter previews; it does not alter the original uploaded file.

field.summary: The time of day the scheduled media storage environment update runs.
field.usage: Sets when the media storage environment synchronization/update is scheduled to run. A global (default-scope) setting.

field.summary: Which configured database connection media files are stored in.
field.usage: Picks the database resource (from the connections defined in the deployment config) used to hold media files. Applies only when Media Storage is set to Database.

field.summary: Where product and catalog media files are stored — the file system or the database.
field.usage: Selects the backend for media files: File System (the default) or Database (Deprecated). Choose Database only for legacy multi-server setups that relied on it; File System is recommended for new stores.

values.value: Store media files on the file system.
Store media files in the database (deprecated).

field.summary: How long failed messages are kept before cleanup removes them.
field.usage: The retention period for messages that failed processing, after which the queue cleanup removes them.

field.summary: How long new, unprocessed messages are kept before cleanup removes them.
field.usage: The retention period for new messages that have not yet been processed, after which the queue cleanup removes them.

field.summary: How long a message may stay in progress before it is retried.
field.usage: The waiting period after which a message still marked as in progress is released and retried, so stalled messages are not lost.

field.summary: How long successfully processed messages are kept before cleanup removes them.
field.usage: The retention period for messages that have been processed successfully, after which the queue cleanup removes them.

field.summary: Caps admin session size in bytes; 0 disables the limit.
field.usage: Maximum size, in bytes, an admin session may reach. Guards against oversized sessions that can trigger errors or slow the admin; as the native note says, 0 removes the cap. Global scope.

field.summary: Caps storefront session size in bytes to curb memory abuse; 0 disables the limit.
field.usage: Caps how large a storefront session may grow, in bytes; sessions that exceed it are rejected to curb runaway growth and memory abuse. Use 0 to remove the limit entirely.

field.summary: The authentication method used to connect to the SMTP server.
field.usage: The SMTP authentication method: NONE, PLAIN, or LOGIN. Applies only when Transport is set to SMTP. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Stops the store from sending any outbound email.
field.usage: When Yes, all outbound email from the store is suppressed. Useful on staging/testing environments to avoid emailing real customers. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Hostname of the SMTP relay Magento hands outgoing mail to; ignored unless the SMTP sending path is in use.
field.usage: The SMTP server Magento connects to for outgoing mail. As the native note implies, it matters only for the SMTP/Windows sending path; if a transactional-email extension or a different transport handles mail, this value is ignored. Can be set per website/store.

field.summary: The password for the SMTP account used to send store email; stored encrypted and used only when the SMTP transport is selected.
field.usage: The password Magento uses to authenticate with your SMTP server when sending outgoing mail. Stored encrypted by the backend model. Applies only when the mail transport is set to SMTP. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: TCP port Magento connects to for sending mail; must match the mail server's listening port.
field.usage: The port used for outgoing SMTP. It must match the port your mail server actually listens on, or mail silently fails to send. Accepts 0–65535 per the native note. Website/store scoped, so stores can use different mail servers.

field.summary: The Return-Path (bounce) address used for outbound email.
field.usage: The address that receives bounce notifications for outbound mail. Applies only when Set Return-Path is set to Specified. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether to set the email Return-Path header, and whether to use a specified address.
field.usage: Controls the Return-Path (bounce) address on outbound mail: No, Yes (use the sender address), or Specified (use the Return-Path Email below). Can differ per website or store view.

values.value: On.
Off.
Use the custom value specified below.

field.summary: The encryption used when connecting to the SMTP server.
field.usage: The connection security for SMTP: None, SSL, or TLS. Applies only when Transport is set to SMTP. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: How outbound mail is sent — via Sendmail or an SMTP server.
field.usage: Selects the mail transport: Sendmail (the local MTA) or SMTP (an external mail server). Choosing SMTP enables the related Auth and SSL settings. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The account name used to authenticate to your SMTP server for outgoing mail; blank means no SMTP login.
field.usage: The username Magento uses to log in to the SMTP server when sending mail. Applies only when the mail transport is SMTP. Leave blank only if the server accepts unauthenticated relay. Set per website or store view so each can send through a different mail account.

field.summary: How aggressively the browser preloads likely next pages; higher is faster but wastes more.
field.usage: Controls how eagerly the browser speculatively loads probable next pages. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled. As the native note says, higher eagerness loads pages sooner but may fetch ones never visited, adding server load and bandwidth. Can differ per scope.

field.summary: Yes uses the browser Speculation Rules API to prefetch/prerender likely next pages for faster navigation; adds speculative server load.
field.usage: When Yes, Magento emits Speculation Rules so supporting browsers prefetch or prerender pages before a link is clicked, making navigation feel faster (native note). The trade-off is extra load from speculative requests, and only modern browsers honour it. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: File extensions excluded from speculative prefetch/prerender; applies only when speculative loading is on.
field.usage: A comma-separated list of file extensions whose URLs are excluded from speculative prefetching/prerendering. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled, and is scoped per store view. Use it to keep downloads or heavy endpoints from being fetched ahead of a click.

field.summary: URL patterns (one per line) kept out of speculative prefetch/prerender, e.g. logout or cart actions.
field.usage: URLs matching these patterns (one per line) are excluded from speculative prefetch and prerender. Use it for logout, add-to-cart or anything with side effects you don't want triggered before the shopper clicks. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled.

technical.default_value: customer login logout auth cart checkout search download redirect rewrite store productalert

field.summary: CSS selectors (one per line) whose links are excluded from speculative prerender/prefetch; applies only when speculative loading is on. Per website/store.
field.usage: Links matching these CSS selectors (one per line) are left out of speculative prerendering/prefetching. Use it to stop prefetching one-shot or state-changing links (logout, add-to-cart, delete) that could fire unintended actions. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled. Per website/store.

field.summary: Picks how aggressively browsers preload next pages; prerender is fastest but can skew analytics.
field.usage: Chooses the speculative-loading strategy browsers use to fetch likely next pages. Prerender is fastest but runs page JS before the page is opened, which can distort analytics unless accounted for. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Yes resizes images in the browser before upload, cutting upload size and server load.
field.usage: When Yes, images are resized via JavaScript in the browser before being uploaded, reducing upload size, transfer time and server-side processing. It relies on client-side JS, so the browser does the work before the file is sent.

field.summary: JPEG compression (1-100) for resized images; higher is sharper but larger. Cached images keep old quality until regenerated.
field.usage: Compression quality applied when Magento resizes or generates JPEGs. Higher values look sharper but produce larger files and slower loads. It affects images generated after the change; already-cached images keep their old quality until the image cache is flushed and regenerated.

field.summary: Caps uploaded image height, scaling taller images down; active only when upload resize is on.
field.usage: Uploaded images taller than this are scaled down on upload, which lowers stored file size and keeps media dimensions consistent. Takes effect only when resize-on-upload is enabled.

field.summary: Caps the width of uploaded images; wider images are scaled down on upload.
field.usage: Maximum pixel width for newly uploaded images. Applies only when image resize on upload is enabled. Oversized uploads are scaled down to save storage and bandwidth; images already stored are not affected.

field.summary: Adds animated transitions between same-domain page loads.
field.usage: When enabled, animates transitions between pages loaded on the same domain for a smoother, app-like feel. Relies on browser support and degrades gracefully where absent. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Whether to enable animated View Transitions in the Admin panel.
field.usage: When Yes, the browser View Transitions API is used to animate navigation within the Admin panel. Set to No to disable the effect.

field.summary: Yes animates back/forward navigation but may forgo the faster Back/Forward Cache restore.
field.usage: Yes animates back/forward navigation with view transitions, but doing so can bypass the browser's Back/Forward Cache that would otherwise restore the page instantly. No keeps that faster cached restore without the animation. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: How tax is rounded — per unit, per row, or on the total.
field.usage: The rounding method for tax: Unit Price (round each item), Row Total (round each line), or Total (round the order total). Affects cent-level differences on multi-item orders.

values.value: Round tax on each unit, then multiply by quantity.
Round tax once per line (row total).
Round tax once on the order total.

field.summary: Whether tax is applied before or after discounts.
field.usage: Chooses whether customer tax is calculated on the price Before Discount or After Discount — this changes the taxable base when promotions apply.

values.value: Apply tax to the price before any discount.
Apply tax to the price after the discount.

field.summary: Whether tax uses the custom price or the original price.
field.usage: Applies tax on the Custom price if available, or always on the Original price, for items with a special/custom price.

values.value: Tax the custom price when one is set, otherwise the original.
Always tax the original price, ignoring custom prices.

field.summary: Which address tax is calculated from.
field.usage: Whether tax is based on the Shipping Address, the Billing Address, or the store's Shipping Origin.

values.value: Calculate tax from the customer's shipping address.
Calculate tax from the customer's billing address.
Calculate tax from the store's shipping origin.

field.summary: Yes keeps tax-inclusive catalog prices identical across regions, absorbing differing tax rates into margin.
field.usage: When catalog prices include tax, setting Yes fixes the displayed price regardless of the customer's tax rate (per the note) — the advertised figure stays constant across regions and the differing tax is absorbed into your margin rather than changing the price. Only meaningful with tax-inclusive pricing. Set per website.

field.summary: Whether discounts apply to prices including or excluding tax; changes the taxable base.
field.usage: Chooses whether cart discounts are calculated on prices including or excluding tax, which shifts the taxable base. As the native note warns, applying the discount on tax-included prices requires Catalog Prices set to Including Tax. Saving flags a tax-configuration notice; website scoped.

values.value: Prices you enter are treated as not including tax.
Prices you enter are treated as already including tax.

field.summary: Whether catalog prices entered in admin already include tax; can differ per website.
field.usage: Tells the tax engine whether catalog prices entered in the admin are tax-inclusive, as the field note says. It changes whether tax is extracted from the entered price or added on top, so switching it shifts the effective shelf prices. Scoped to website.

values.value: Prices you enter are treated as not including tax.
Prices you enter are treated as already including tax.

field.summary: Declares whether entered/gateway shipping amounts already include tax; getting it wrong double-counts or omits shipping tax. Per website.
field.usage: Tells Magento whether shipping amounts (entered in admin or returned by carriers) already contain tax. If this is set wrong, shipping tax is either double-counted or dropped. Changing it alters how the shipping tax base is computed on new calculations. Scoped per website.

values.value: Prices you enter are treated as not including tax.
Prices you enter are treated as already including tax.

field.summary: Whether the cart breaks tax down by rate instead of a single line.
field.usage: When Yes, the cart shows a full tax summary (each tax rate itemised) rather than one combined tax line.

field.summary: Whether the cart also shows the order total without tax.
field.usage: When Yes, the cart additionally shows the grand total excluding tax alongside the taxed total.

field.summary: Whether cart item prices show including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Price display for items in the shopping cart: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

values.value: Show prices with tax left out.
Show prices with tax already included.
Show both the tax-excluded and tax-included price.

field.summary: Whether the cart shipping amount shows including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Shipping-amount display in the cart: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

values.value: Show prices with tax left out.
Show prices with tax already included.
Show both the tax-excluded and tax-included price.

field.summary: Whether the cart subtotal shows including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Subtotal display in the cart: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

values.value: Show prices with tax left out.
Show prices with tax already included.
Show both the tax-excluded and tax-included price.

field.summary: Whether a zero-value tax line is shown in the cart.
field.usage: When Yes, a tax line is shown even when the tax amount is zero; when No, it is hidden.

field.summary: The tax class assigned to a customer group when none is set.
field.usage: The default customer tax class, used together with the product tax class to resolve the applicable tax rate.

field.summary: The tax class assigned to a new product when none is set.
field.usage: The default product tax class used for products that don't specify one, determining which tax rates apply to them.

field.summary: The tax class applied to shipping charges.
field.usage: Which product tax class shipping is taxed under. Pick the class whose rates should apply to the shipping amount (or a 'None' class to leave shipping untaxed).

field.summary: Default country used to estimate tax before a customer address is known.
field.usage: The fallback destination country for tax estimation (e.g. catalog prices) until the customer provides an address.

field.summary: Default post code used to estimate tax before a customer address is known.
field.usage: The fallback destination post code for tax estimation. Use * to match any post code within the default region.

field.summary: Default state/region used to estimate tax before a customer address is known.
field.usage: The fallback destination state/region for tax estimation, paired with the Default Country.

field.summary: Whether shipping prices show including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: How shipping amounts are displayed in the catalog/estimates: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

values.value: Show prices with tax left out.
Show prices with tax already included.
Show both the tax-excluded and tax-included price.

field.summary: Whether catalog prices show including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: How product prices appear in the catalog: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

values.value: Show prices with tax left out.
Show prices with tax already included.
Show both the tax-excluded and tax-included price.

field.summary: Whether sales documents break tax down by rate instead of a single line.
field.usage: When Yes, sales documents show a full tax summary (each rate itemised) rather than one combined tax line.

field.summary: Whether sales documents also show the order total without tax.
field.usage: When Yes, orders, invoices and credit memos additionally show the grand total excluding tax.

field.summary: Whether prices on orders, invoices and credit memos show including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Price display on sales documents (orders, invoices, credit memos): Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

values.value: Show prices with tax left out.
Show prices with tax already included.
Show both the tax-excluded and tax-included price.

field.summary: Whether the shipping amount on sales documents shows including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Shipping-amount display on orders, invoices and credit memos: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

values.value: Show prices with tax left out.
Show prices with tax already included.
Show both the tax-excluded and tax-included price.

field.summary: Whether the subtotal on sales documents shows including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Subtotal display on orders, invoices and credit memos: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

values.value: Show prices with tax left out.
Show prices with tax already included.
Show both the tax-excluded and tax-included price.

field.summary: Whether a zero-value tax line is shown on sales documents.
field.usage: When Yes, a tax line is shown on orders, invoices and credit memos even when the tax amount is zero.

field.summary: Whether tax is also applied on top of the Fixed Product Tax amount.
field.usage: When Yes, regular tax is calculated on the FPT amount as well as on the product price. Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

field.summary: How Fixed Product Tax amounts are shown on the product view page.
field.usage: Controls the way FPT amounts are displayed on the product detail page. Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

values.value: Show the price including the fixed product tax, with no separate line.
Show the price including the fee, plus a line describing it.

value.label: Excluding FPT. Including FPT description and final price

values.value: Show the price without the fee, plus the fee description and final price.
Show the price with the fixed product tax left out.

field.summary: How Fixed Product Tax amounts are shown in emails.
field.usage: Controls the way FPT amounts are displayed in transactional emails. Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

values.value: Show the price including the fixed product tax, with no separate line.
Show the price including the fee, plus a line describing it.

value.label: Excluding FPT. Including FPT description and final price

values.value: Show the price without the fee, plus the fee description and final price.
Show the price with the fixed product tax left out.

field.summary: How Fixed Product Tax amounts are shown in product lists.
field.usage: Controls the way FPT amounts appear in category and other product lists (for example shown separately or rolled into the price). Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

values.value: Show the price including the fixed product tax, with no separate line.
Show the price including the fee, plus a line describing it.

value.label: Excluding FPT. Including FPT description and final price

values.value: Show the price without the fee, plus the fee description and final price.
Show the price with the fixed product tax left out.

field.summary: How Fixed Product Tax amounts are shown in sales documents.
field.usage: Controls the way FPT amounts are displayed in sales areas such as the cart, orders and invoices. Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

values.value: Show the price including the fixed product tax, with no separate line.
Show the price including the fee, plus a line describing it.

value.label: Excluding FPT. Including FPT description and final price

values.value: Show the price without the fee, plus the fee description and final price.
Show the price with the fixed product tax left out.

field.summary: Turns Fixed Product Tax (FPT) calculation on or off.
field.usage: When set to Yes, Fixed Product Tax (FPT) is calculated and applied to products that carry an FPT attribute. Can be set per website, so FPT can be active on one website and off on another.
