field.summary: Whether the Fixed Product Tax is included in the order subtotal.
field.usage: When Yes, FPT is added into the order subtotal rather than shown as a separate amount. Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The CardinalCommerce API Identifier used to authenticate 3-D Secure requests.
field.usage: The API Identifier credential issued by CardinalCommerce. Stored encrypted. Applies only when the integration is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The CardinalCommerce API key used to authenticate 3-D Secure requests.
field.usage: The API key credential issued by CardinalCommerce. Stored encrypted. Applies only when the integration is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether CardinalCommerce request and response details are written to the debug log.
field.usage: When Yes, CardinalCommerce communication is logged for troubleshooting. Applies only when the integration is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether CardinalCommerce 3-D Secure requests use the sandbox or production environment.
field.usage: Selects the CardinalCommerce target: Sandbox for testing or Production for live transactions. Applies only when the CardinalCommerce integration is enabled. Can differ per website.

values.value: Use the Cardinal sandbox for testing.
Use the live Cardinal environment.

field.summary: The CardinalCommerce Org Unit ID used to authenticate 3-D Secure requests.
field.usage: The Org Unit ID credential issued by CardinalCommerce for the Cardinal Cruise API. Stored encrypted. Applies only when the integration is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The 'From' email address for the Custom Email 1 store identity.
field.usage: The sender email address used when the Custom Email 1 identity is selected as the sender of a transactional email. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' display name for the Custom Email 1 store identity.
field.usage: The sender name shown on emails sent from the Custom Email 1 identity. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' email address for the Custom Email 2 store identity.
field.usage: The sender email address used when the Custom Email 2 identity is selected as the sender of a transactional email. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' display name for the Custom Email 2 store identity.
field.usage: The sender name shown on emails sent from the Custom Email 2 identity. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' email address for the General Contact store identity.
field.usage: The sender email address for the General Contact identity, the default sender for many store notifications. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' display name for the General Contact store identity.
field.usage: The sender name shown on emails sent from the General Contact identity. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' email address for the Sales Representative store identity.
field.usage: The sender email address for the Sales Representative identity, used as the sender of sales-related emails. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' display name for the Sales Representative store identity.
field.usage: The sender name shown on emails sent from the Sales Representative identity. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' email address for the Customer Support store identity.
field.usage: The sender email address for the Customer Support identity, used as the sender of support-related emails. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' display name for the Customer Support store identity.
field.usage: The sender name shown on emails sent from the Customer Support identity. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The API key of your Authy account, used for Authy two-factor authentication; stored encrypted.
field.usage: The Authy API key that this store uses to send and verify Authy two-factor challenges. It is stored encrypted. Obtain it from your Authy/Twilio account.

field.summary: The approval message shown to users in Authy OneTouch push requests.
field.usage: The text displayed in the Authy OneTouch approval prompt that users receive when signing in. Use it to identify the request.

technical.default_value: Login request to your Magento Admin

field.summary: The API hostname of your Duo Security account.
field.usage: The Duo API hostname (for example the api-….duosecurity.com host from your Duo admin panel) that this store contacts for the Duo Universal Prompt.

field.summary: The Client ID of your Duo Security application, used for the Duo Universal Prompt.
field.usage: Identifies the Duo Security application that authenticates admin sign-ins via the Duo Universal Prompt. Obtain it from your Duo admin panel and enter it here.

field.summary: The Client Secret of your Duo Security application; stored encrypted.
field.usage: The secret paired with the Duo Client Id for the Duo Universal Prompt. It is stored encrypted. Obtain it from your Duo admin panel.

field.summary: The integration key of your Duo Security application.
field.usage: The integration key issued for the Duo application used by the Duo Universal Prompt. Obtain it from your Duo admin panel.

field.summary: The secret key of your Duo Security application; stored encrypted.
field.usage: The secret key paired with the Duo Integration Key. It is stored encrypted. Obtain it from your Duo admin panel.

field.summary: How long a user is locked out after hitting the failed-2FA threshold; longer deters brute-force attempts.
field.usage: Time, in seconds, a user stays locked out once they reach the failed two-factor-attempt threshold. Longer periods deter brute-forcing codes; shorter ones reduce lockout frustration. Must be between 120 and 1800 (30 minutes).

field.summary: Which 2FA methods admin users are allowed to use at login.
field.usage: Restricts the two-factor authentication methods admin users may use when signing in. Selecting several providers lets each admin choose among them; narrowing to one enforces that method for everyone. Default scope — it applies to all admins.

values.value: Time-based codes via Google Authenticator.
Push/approval via Duo Security.
Codes or push via Authy.
Hardware security key (U2F — YubiKey and similar).

field.summary: How many 2FA attempts are allowed before a temporary lockout; lower resists code-guessing but risks locking out admins who mistype.
field.usage: Sets how many times an admin can attempt the two-factor step before a temporary lockout (native note). Lower values harden against code-guessing; set it too low and legitimate admins who mistype get locked out. Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Custom URL for the 2FA setup link in Web API auth emails; must include the :tfat placeholder for the token.
field.usage: Overrides the default 2FA configuration link sent in Web API authentication emails, pointing it at a URL you choose (per the note). It must contain the :tfat placeholder marking where the token is injected, or the generated link won't work. Default scope.

field.summary: Clock-drift tolerance (seconds) for Google Authenticator OTPs; must be below the period.
field.usage: Seconds of clock-drift tolerance when validating Google Authenticator OTPs, and must stay below the OTP period (see the native example). A larger leeway accepts more server/device time skew but widens the window each code stays valid, a small security trade-off.

field.summary: WebAuthn domain for U2F key challenges via Web API; must match registration or auth fails.
field.usage: The WebAuthn relying-party domain used when issuing and verifying U2F security-key challenges over the Web API. It must match the domain where keys were registered or authentication fails; leave blank to use the store domain.

field.summary: Whether dynamically-defined attributes are exposed as fields on their entity types in the GraphQL schema.
field.usage: When Yes, dynamic (store-defined) attributes appear as typed fields on their entity in the GraphQL schema rather than only through generic containers. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether visitors with cookies disabled are redirected to the No Cookies CMS page.
field.usage: When Yes, visitors whose browsers have cookies disabled are redirected to the configured CMS No Cookies page. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether a notice is shown to visitors who have JavaScript disabled.
field.usage: When Yes, a notice is displayed to visitors whose browsers have JavaScript disabled. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether a notice is shown to visitors who have local storage disabled.
field.usage: When Yes, a notice is displayed to visitors whose browsers have local storage disabled. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Domain cookies are issued for; a mismatch with the real site domain breaks login and sessions.
field.usage: Scopes session and other cookies to a domain. It must match the domain customers actually use (a leading dot shares across subdomains); a mismatch silently breaks sessions and login. Leave empty to use the current domain. Website/store scoped for multi-domain stores.

field.summary: Yes sets the HttpOnly flag so scripts can't read cookies; No exposes session cookies to XSS — don't.
field.usage: When Yes, cookies carry the HttpOnly flag, so client-side JavaScript cannot read them — this blocks session theft via cross-site scripting. The native warning is serious: No leaves session cookies readable by scripts. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: How long cookies persist, in seconds; shorter values log customers out sooner. Can differ per store view.
field.usage: The cookie lifetime in seconds, as the field note states. A shorter value expires sessions and stored preferences sooner (more frequent re-logins), a longer one keeps them around. Scoped to website/store, so it can vary per store view.

field.summary: Scopes cookies to a URL path; set narrower than / only if the store runs in a subfolder, or logins and cart break. Needs a cache flush.
field.usage: Restricts the browser to send Magento cookies only under this path. Leave it at / for most stores; narrowing it is right only when the store runs in a subdirectory, otherwise sessions, login and cart silently fail. Takes effect after a cache flush; settable per website/store.

field.summary: Yes enables cookie-consent mode: visitors are told cookies are needed and some are withheld until accepted (GDPR/privacy compliance).
field.usage: When Yes, Cookie Restriction Mode shows storefront visitors a consent notice (native note) and holds back non-essential cookies until they accept — used to meet GDPR and similar privacy requirements. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The CMS page shown as the storefront home page.
field.usage: Selects which existing CMS page is used as the storefront home page. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The CMS page shown when the visitor's browser has cookies disabled.
field.usage: Selects the CMS page displayed when a visitor's browser has cookies disabled. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The CMS page shown when a requested page is not found (404).
field.usage: Selects the CMS page displayed when a URL does not match any route, i.e. a 404. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The default storefront landing path used when no specific route is requested.
field.usage: The route the storefront falls back to for the home page when no path is given (typically cms). Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The default page layout for category pages.
field.usage: The layout applied to category pages that don't specify their own.

field.summary: The default page layout applied to CMS pages.
field.usage: The layout (for example 1 column or 2 columns) used by default for CMS pages that do not specify their own.

field.summary: The default page layout for product pages.
field.usage: The layout (e.g. 1 column, 2 columns left/right, 3 columns) applied to product pages that don't specify their own.

field.summary: The path served when a requested URL matches no route (the 404 page).
field.usage: The internal path rendered when a URL cannot be matched to any route, i.e. the 'page not found' target. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether breadcrumb navigation is shown on CMS pages.
field.usage: When Yes, breadcrumb navigation is displayed on CMS pages. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: HTTPS base for building storefront links; use the placeholder to track the base URL automatically.
field.usage: The HTTPS base used to build links on the storefront. Using the {{secure_base_url}}/{{unsecure_base_url}} placeholder keeps it in step with the base URL instead of hardcoding it. Can differ per website or store view; a wrong value breaks generated secure links.

field.summary: Points secure user/media files at a host or CDN; blank derives it from the secure base URL. Must end in a slash and needs a cache flush.
field.usage: Sets where secure user media files are served from, e.g. a CDN or separate media host. Leave it empty (or use the {{secure_base_url}}/{{unsecure_base_url}} placeholders) to derive it from the base URL. A missing trailing slash breaks asset paths, and changes apply only after a cache flush. Per website/store.

field.summary: Overrides where static view files are served over HTTPS, e.g. a CDN; can differ per store view.
field.usage: Sets the HTTPS base URL for static view files (CSS, JS, fonts), typically to point them at a CDN. As the field note says, it may be empty or use the {{secure_base_url}} / {{unsecure_base_url}} placeholders. Scoped to website/store, so each store view can use a different host.

field.summary: The HTTPS base URL for storefront pages, links and assets; supports {{base_url}} placeholders.
field.usage: Base HTTPS URL for secure pages, links and static assets. Can differ per website/store view for multi-domain setups. A wrong value breaks secure pages and asset loading; flush caches after changing. Placeholders such as {{base_url}} are accepted.

field.summary: Yes sends the HSTS header telling browsers to use HTTPS only; enable only once HTTPS fully works, as browsers then refuse HTTP.
field.usage: When Yes, Magento sends the HTTP Strict Transport Security header, instructing browsers to connect only over HTTPS and blocking downgrade attacks. Requires secure URLs on both storefront and admin (depends). Browsers cache it for its max-age, so enable only once HTTPS is fully working. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Adds a header so browsers auto-upgrade http asset requests to https, avoiding mixed-content warnings.
field.usage: When Yes, sends the upgrade-insecure-requests CSP directive so browsers automatically fetch http assets over https, preventing mixed-content blocks. Relevant only when secure URLs are used on the storefront and admin. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: The HTTP header used to detect that SSL is terminated by a load balancer or proxy.
field.usage: The request header (e.g. X-Forwarded-Proto) that the store reads to recognise HTTPS when SSL is offloaded to a proxy or load balancer rather than handled by the web server directly.

field.summary: Yes forces the Admin over HTTPS; needs a valid cert on the secure base URL or you risk locking yourself out.
field.usage: When Yes, the Admin panel is served over HTTPS so login and session cookies are encrypted. Gotcha: this requires a working SSL certificate on the secure base URL (enter the https protocol, per the note) — if it's missing you can lock yourself out of the Admin. Default scope.

field.summary: Forces the storefront onto HTTPS using the Secure Base URL; needs a valid certificate.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront is served over HTTPS via the Secure Base URL. That URL must use the https protocol and have a valid certificate, or customers hit errors. Website/store scoped, so you can secure specific store views.

field.summary: Removes index.php from storefront URLs using web server rewrites.
field.usage: When Yes, URLs are generated without index.php, relying on the web server's rewrite rules (e.g. Apache mod_rewrite or Nginx). Enable only when rewrites are configured on the server. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Validates the browser's HTTP_USER_AGENT for the session, as anti-hijacking protection.
field.usage: When Yes, the session is tied to the request's HTTP_USER_AGENT and invalidated if it changes, guarding against session hijacking.

field.summary: Validates the HTTP_VIA header for the session, as anti-hijacking protection.
field.usage: When Yes, the session is tied to the request's HTTP_VIA header and invalidated if it changes. May cause issues behind some proxies.

field.summary: Validates the HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR header for the session, as anti-hijacking protection.
field.usage: When Yes, the session is tied to the request's HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR header and invalidated if it changes. May cause issues behind some proxies/load balancers.

field.summary: Validates that a session's client IP (REMOTE_ADDR) stays consistent, as anti-hijacking protection.
field.usage: When Yes, the session is bound to the client's REMOTE_ADDR and invalidated if it changes, guarding against session hijacking. May cause issues behind some proxies/NAT.

field.summary: Base HTTP URL used to build storefront links; the {{unsecure_base_url}} placeholder keeps it tied to your main base URL.
field.usage: The base address Magento uses to build non-secure (HTTP) links to store pages. The {{unsecure_base_url}} placeholder (per the note) keeps it derived from the main base URL so you set the domain once. Changing it affects all generated links. Set per website or store view for multi-domain setups.

field.summary: Where the storefront loads media from; point it at a CDN or separate host to offload image traffic.
field.usage: Base URL the storefront uses for user media files such as product images. Set it to a CDN or dedicated media host to offload asset traffic from the web server. May be empty or start with the {{unsecure_base_url}} placeholder. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: HTTP base URL for static view files (CSS/JS/images); set it to a CDN to offload assets, or leave empty to inherit the base URL.
field.usage: The base URL from which static view files (CSS, JavaScript, images) are served over HTTP. Point it at a CDN to serve assets from a separate host; leave empty or use the {{unsecure_base_url}} placeholder to inherit the store base URL. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Root HTTP URL for building storefront links and assets; a wrong value can break the whole site.
field.usage: The base for all non-secure (http) URLs — links, images, scripts. You may use the {{base_url}} placeholder. An incorrect value breaks asset loading and can lock you out, and changes usually need a cache flush. Website/store scoped for multi-domain setups.

field.summary: Chooses image-proxy vs legacy catalog media URLs; switching back to legacy needs a CLI image regen.
field.usage: Selects how catalog image URLs are built: a query-parameter format your CDN/web server optimizes, or the legacy per-size path for backward compatibility. As the field note warns, switching back to legacy means you must regenerate images via the CLI before they appear correctly.

value.label: Image optimization based on query parameters

values.value: Serve image variants via query parameters (CDN-friendly).

value.label: Unique hash per image variant (Legacy mode)

values.value: Serve each variant as a uniquely hashed file (legacy).

field.summary: Forces visitors onto the canonical base host to avoid duplicate URLs and split sessions; choose off, or a temporary vs permanent redirect.
field.usage: Redirects requests arriving on a non-canonical host to your configured base URL, preventing duplicate-content and split-session problems. The options let you disable it or pick a temporary versus a permanent redirect; a permanent one is cached hard by browsers and search engines, so test before enabling. Per website/store.

values.value: Do not redirect between base URLs.
Redirect with a temporary 302 (Found).
Redirect with a permanent 301 (Moved Permanently).

field.summary: Adds the store code to storefront URLs; changing it rewrites every storefront link.
field.usage: When Yes, the active store code is inserted into storefront URLs so different store views are addressable. As the field note warns, hard-coded URLs without a store code in third-party services (e.g. PayPal) may then break, so change it with care.

field.summary: Whether to disable PHP session handling for GraphQL requests.
field.usage: When Yes, GraphQL requests are served without starting a PHP session, which can improve performance for stateless API traffic.

field.summary: Whether to enforce a maximum number of field aliases in a GraphQL query.
field.usage: When Yes, GraphQL queries using more than the allowed number of aliases are rejected, limiting a known request-amplification technique. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether to enforce configured limits on GraphQL query input size.
field.usage: When Yes, the configured GraphQL input limits are enforced, rejecting queries that exceed them. A safeguard against overly large or abusive queries. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Caps aliases per GraphQL request to curb abuse; set too low and legitimate queries fail.
field.usage: Limits how many aliases a single GraphQL request may use, a guard against resource-exhaustion attacks. Applies only when the alias limit is enabled. Set it too low and complex but legitimate queries are rejected. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Caps pageSize on GraphQL queries to block expensive requests; applies only when input limits are on. Too low breaks large listings.
field.usage: Upper bound on how many items a single paginated GraphQL query may request, protecting the server from oversized or expensive calls. Applies only when GraphQL input limits are enabled; setting it below what the storefront asks for will make those queries fail. Per website/store.

field.summary: Max characters allowed in a GraphQL request; longer queries are rejected. Applies only when the length limit is on.
field.usage: The maximum number of characters a GraphQL query string may contain; larger requests are rejected. It guards against oversized or abusive queries. Applies only when the GraphQL query-length limit is enabled. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether to enforce a maximum character length for GraphQL queries.
field.usage: When Yes, GraphQL queries longer than the allowed character count are rejected. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Lifetime in minutes of an admin API JWT before it must be reissued.
field.usage: How long, in minutes, an admin user's JWT stays valid for API calls. Shorter lifetimes limit the damage of a leaked token but force more frequent re-authentication; longer ones are more convenient but riskier. Default scope only.

field.summary: Lifetime, in minutes, of customer JWT access tokens; shorter is more secure but forces more frequent re-authentication.
field.usage: How long, in minutes, a customer's JWT access token stays valid. A shorter lifetime limits the damage from a stolen token but makes customers and clients re-authenticate more often; a longer one is more convenient but riskier.

field.summary: Content-encryption algorithm used when API tokens are issued as encrypted JWEs.
field.usage: Selects the algorithm that encrypts the payload of JWT tokens. As the field note says, it takes effect when a JWE (encrypted) algorithm is in use rather than a plain signed token, keeping the token contents opaque to the client.

field.summary: Algorithm for auth JWTs; signing gives a readable JWS, encryption a confidential JWE.
field.usage: The algorithm used to sign or encrypt authentication JWTs. A signing algorithm produces a JWS (tamper-evident but readable); an encryption algorithm produces a JWE (also confidential). It must match what your API clients expect or tokens are rejected.

field.summary: Character set declared on SOAP API responses; empty uses UTF-8. Change only if a client needs another encoding.
field.usage: The character set declared on SOAP Web API responses; left empty, UTF-8 is used (per the note). Change it only when a consuming client requires a different encoding, since UTF-8 is the safe default for most integrations. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Maximum items allowed in an array property of a Web API request, blocking oversized payloads; applies only when input limiting is on.
field.usage: Caps how many elements an array property may contain in a Web API request body, guarding against oversized or abusive payloads (native note). Applies only when Web API input limits are enabled (depends). Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Default page size for API search results when the client doesn't specify one.
field.usage: Number of records returned per page for REST/GraphQL search results when the request omits a page size. Larger values mean fewer round-trips but heavier responses and more memory per call. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Whether Web API requests enforce limits on the size of input arrays and collections.
field.usage: When Yes, the Web API enforces input limits, such as the maximum number of items accepted in a request, rejecting oversized payloads to protect the store. Configured under Magento Web API → Web Api Input Limits.

field.summary: Caps items per page on API searches to block oversized, expensive requests; only when input limits are on.
field.usage: Maximum number of items allowed in a paginated API search result, preventing oversized and resource-heavy requests. Enforced only when API input limits are enabled. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Permits anonymous access to normally-protected CMS, Catalog and Store APIs; a security risk.
field.usage: When Yes, allows unauthenticated access to API resources that are otherwise protected, limited to CMS, Catalog and Store APIs per the native note. It exposes data without auth, so review the risk with developers before enabling. Default scope.

field.summary: Which store email identity wish list sharing emails are sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity used when a customer shares a wish list by email — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2). Can differ per store view.

values.value: Send as the General Contact store identity.
Send as the Sales Representative store identity.
Send as the Customer Support store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 1 store identity.
Send as the Custom Email 2 store identity.

field.summary: Template for the shared wish-list email; Default follows theme fallback.
field.usage: The template for the email sent when a customer shares their wish list. Default follows theme fallback; a custom template overrides it. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Caps how many recipients a single wishlist-share email can have; can differ per store view.
field.usage: The maximum number of recipient addresses allowed when sharing a wish list by email. As the field note says, the default is 10 and the ceiling is 10000. Scoped to website/store, so each store view can set its own limit.

field.summary: Max characters in the personal message when a wishlist is shared (255 by default, up to 10000); raising it allows longer notes. Per website/store.
field.usage: Caps the length of the personal message a customer can add when sharing a wish list, 255 by default and up to 10000. Raising it permits longer notes at some added risk of abuse/spam. Settable per website/store.

field.summary: Turns the storefront wish list feature on or off.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can add products to a wish list; No disables the feature. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether the wish list block appears in the storefront sidebar.
field.usage: When Yes, a wish list block is shown in the storefront sidebar. Applies only when Enabled (wish list) is set to Yes. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: What the My Wish List link summary displays for its contents.
field.usage: Controls how the My Wish List link summarises the list's contents (such as item count versus quantity). Can differ per website.

value.label: Display number of items in wish list

values.value: Show the count of items in the wish-list summary.
Show the total quantity of units in the wish-list summary.
